XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yn y fersiwn ddwyieithog, mae’r golofn chwith yn cynnwys yr iaith a lefarwyd yn y cyfarfod. Mae’r golofn dde yn cynnwys cyfieithiad o’r areithiau hynny.

Mae [R] yn dynodi bod yr Aelod wedi datgan buddiant wrth gyflwyno’r busnes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
In the bilingual version, the left-hand column includes the language used during the meeting. The right-hand column includes a translation of those speeches.

[R] indicates that the Member has declared an interest when tabling the business.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cyfarfu'r Senedd yn y Siambr a thrwy gynhadledd fideo am 13:30 gyda'r Dirprwy Lywydd (Kerry Ferguson) yn y Gadair.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Senedd met in the Chamber and by video-conference at 13:30 with the Dirprwy Lywydd (Kerry Ferguson) in the Chair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prynhawn da a chroeso i'r Siambr. Eitem 1 ar yr agenda, cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal. Cwestiwn 1, Anna Nicholl.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Good afternoon and welcome to the Chamber. Item 1 on our agenda is questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care. Question 1, Anna Nicholl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa gamau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i gefnogi gofal integredig mewn ardaloedd gwledig? OQ64669
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What action is the Government taking to support integrated care in rural areas? OQ64669

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn. Yn unol â'n hymrwymiad ni yn y rhaglen lywodraethu, mae ein fframwaith system gofal cymunedol integredig yn dod â phartneriaid o'r sectorau iechyd, gofal cymdeithasol, tai a'r trydydd sector ynghyd i edrych ar anghenion lleol. Drwy'r gronfa integreiddio rhanbarthol a'r gronfa gyfalaf integreiddio ac ailgydbwyso, rydyn ni’n cefnogi gwasanaethau ataliol, gofal yn agosach at y cartref a chanolfannau lles integredig, gan gynnwys mewn cymunedau gwledig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: In line with our programme for government commitment, our integrated community care system framework brings health, social care, housing and third-sector partners together around local needs. Through the regional integration fund and integration and rebalancing capital fund, we are supporting preventative services, care closer to home and integrated well-being hubs, including in rural communities.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Weinidog Cabinet, dwi eisoes wedi codi pa mor bwysig yw canolfannau gofal integredig wrth ddarparu gofal yn agosach i gartref. Ond gall system integredig ddim llwyddo heb isadeiledd gofal sylfaenol cynaliadwy. Yn rhy aml, mae meddygfeydd yn gweithio o hen adeiladau sydd ddim wedi eu dylunio ar gyfer gwasanaethau rydym ni bellach yn ei disgwyl. Ac mae fy etholwyr yn cysylltu nid yn unig ynglŷn â'r anhawster o gael apwyntiad meddyg, ond am feddygfeydd yn cau i lawr yn gyfan gwbl. Dwi wedi clywed y gofidion yma gan etholwyr yn Nhyddewi, Cei Newydd, Solfach, Doc Penfro, ac ar draws Ceredigion Penfro. O ystyried ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth i atal a lleihau pwysau ar ysbytai, ydy'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn cytuno y dylid gweld buddsoddiad mewn gofal sylfaenol fel rhan greiddiol o ofal integredig?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. Cabinet Minister. I have already raised how important integrated care centres are in providing care closer to home, but an integrated system cannot succeed without a sustainable primary care infrastructure. Too often, surgeries operate from old buildings that have not been designed for the services that we now expect. And my constituents get in touch with me not only because of the difficulties in getting a doctor's appointment, but as a result of surgeries closing completely. I have heard these concerns from constituents in St David's, Solva, Pembroke Dock and across Ceredigion Penfro. Given the Government's commitment to preventing and reducing pressure on hospitals, does the Cabinet Minister agree that investment in primary care should be seen as a core part of integrated care?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Ddirprwy Lywydd, mae'r Aelod yn gwneud pwynt pwysig yn fanna o ran rôl gofal integredig yn agosach i gartref ac, wrth gwrs, dyna rydym ni'n trio ei wneud ar hyn o bryd. Mi rydyn ni wedi delifro ar yr ymrwymiad a wnaethom ni yn ystod y 100 diwrnod cyntaf er mwyn cael y byrddau iechyd i ddatblygu cynlluniau er mwyn sifftio'r adnoddau i'r gymuned—0.5 y cant o'r ariannu blynyddol yna ydy'r gofyniad, ac maen nhw'n dod â chynlluniau ger fy mron i cyn bo hir. Dwi wedi ei wneud yn glir mai'r disgwyliad ydy eu bod nhw'n gwneud hynny yn fuan.

Un o'r ymrwymiadau wnaethom ni yn y rhaglen lywodraethu, os ydych chi'n cofio, Ddirprwy Lywydd, ydy sicrhau bod mwy o ofal integredig yn cael ei ddelifro yn agosach i gartref er mwyn sicrhau gofal yn agosach i gartref, gofal ataliol yna, mwy o gefnogaeth diagnosis cynt, ac atal pobl rhag mynd i'r ysbyty. Felly, mae hynna'n rhan ganolog o'r hyn rydym ni'n ei wneud.

Mi ydyn ni wedi sicrhau bod yna ddatblygiad yn mynd i fod yn sir Benfro, yn ardal yr Aelod, gydag arian cyfalaf o £1.6 miliwn yn cael ei roi i Fwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Hywel Dda er mwyn datblygu cynllun busnes ar gyfer canolfan o'r fath yn Abergwaun, a dwi'n edrych ymlaen at weld y cynlluniau yn dod ger fy mron. Byddwn i'n hapus i gadw'r Aelod yn wybyddus o beth sy'n digwydd os ydy hi'n dymuno. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you. Dirprwy Lywydd, the Member makes an important point there in terms of the role of integrated care closer to home, and, of course, that's what we're trying to do at the moment. We have delivered on the commitment that we made during our first 100 days in order to get the health boards to develop plans to shift resources into the community—0.5 per cent of that annual funding is the requirement, and they are bringing plans before me soon. I have made it clear that the expectation is that they should do that soon.

One of the commitments that we made in the programme for government, if you recall, Dirprwy Lywydd, was to ensure that more integrated care is delivered closer to home in order to ensure care closer to home, preventative services, increasing earlier diagnostic services, and to prevent people from having to go to hospital. So, that's a central part of what we are doing.

We have ensured that there will be development in Pembrokeshire, in the area covered by the Member, with capital investment of £1.6 million provided to Hywel Dda University Health Board in order to develop a business case for such a centre in Fishguard, and I look forward to seeing those plans come before me. I would be happy to keep the Member informed of developments if she wishes. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Minister, and it's good to hear that you are talking about integrated care, because you know that's something I'm incredibly passionate about, as we've spoken about it.

But today, obviously, I want to talk about something a little bit different, which is that you've increasingly promoted digital and remote health services as a pathway to improving access to care. However, many residents in rural parts of Ceredigion Penfro continue to face poor mobile coverage and unreliable broadband, leading to barriers to using digital technology. Can the Minister explain how the Government is ensuring that the expansion of digital healthcare does not disadvantage rural patients? And what assessment has been made as to whether people in west Wales can access services equally, regardless of where they live? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog, ac mae'n dda eich clywed yn sôn am ofal integredig, gan y gwyddoch fod hynny'n rhywbeth rwy'n angerddol iawn amdano, gan ein bod wedi siarad amdano.

Ond heddiw, yn amlwg, hoffwn sôn am rywbeth ychydig yn wahanol, sef eich bod chi wedi hyrwyddo gwasanaethau iechyd digidol ac o bell yn gynyddol fel llwybr i wella mynediad at ofal. Fodd bynnag, mae llawer o drigolion mewn rhannau gwledig o Geredigion Penfro yn parhau i wynebu signal ffonau symudol gwael a band eang annibynadwy, gan arwain at rwystrau i ddefnyddio technoleg ddigidol. A all y Gweinidog esbonio sut y mae'r Llywodraeth yn sicrhau nad yw'r broses o ehangu gofal iechyd digidol yn rhoi cleifion gwledig o dan anfantais? A pha asesiad a wnaed o allu pobl yn y gorllewin i gael mynediad cyfartal at wasanaethau, ble bynnag y maent yn byw? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thanks for that. You do make a very important point about accessibility in rural communities, or the lack of accessibility. That's why this Government has put forward the rural-proofing plan, so that, whenever a policy is developed or whenever anything is initiated from this Government, it is rural-proofed—we ensure that rurality is considered when rolling that out. And that applies to discussions around mobile coverage as well as everything else.

When it comes to digital connectivity, Hywel Dda is ahead of the game in many respects when it comes to ensuring that we have improved digital connectivity and digital systems in the health board. What we need to see is that the digital systems that we've got in Hywel Dda are linked with social care as well and linked with other national health services. That is a weakness in the system. That's something we're looking at as part of the 10-year digital health programme.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am hynny. Rydych chi'n gwneud pwynt pwysig iawn ynglŷn â hygyrchedd mewn cymunedau gwledig, neu ddiffyg hygyrchedd. Dyna pam y mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi cyflwyno'r cynllun prawfesur gwledig, er mwyn sicrhau, pryd bynnag y datblygir polisi neu y cychwynnir unrhyw beth gan y Llywodraeth hon, ei fod yn addas ar gyfer cefn gwlad—rydym yn sicrhau bod gwledigrwydd yn cael ei ystyried wrth ei gyflwyno. Ac mae hynny'n berthnasol i drafodaethau ynghylch signal ffonau symudol yn ogystal â phopeth arall.

O ran cysylltedd digidol, mae bwrdd Hywel Dda ar y blaen mewn sawl ffordd o ran sicrhau bod gennym well cysylltedd digidol a systemau digidol yn y bwrdd iechyd. Yr hyn sydd angen i ni ei weld yw bod y systemau digidol sydd gennym ym mwrdd Hywel Dda wedi'u cysylltu â gofal cymdeithasol hefyd ac wedi'u cysylltu â gwasanaethau iechyd gwladol eraill. Mae hynny'n wendid yn y system. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth rydym yn edrych arno yn rhan o'r rhaglen iechyd ddigidol 10 mlynedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, the energy pressure that is affecting the whole economy is immense at the moment. The care and health sector are feeling those pressures more acutely than most, given the environment they work in, and especially in a rural setting, where fuel for hospital transport, for example, is a big component of delivering that service. In 2022, when we had the last energy spike, the then health Minister said that the health service and social care sector had just had an unexpected energy bill of £200 million plus because of the Ukrainian crisis. Are you seeing those sorts of figures feeding through because of the crisis in the gulf, given that they happened at virtually the same time of year, in the February of that year, and we're now in the autumn? And if that energy pressure is building, and costing that much money to the health and social care sector, are you making a request to the finance Minister to support health boards and social care providers to meet these energy costs, or will they be expected to use their budgets as allocated?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae'r pwysau ynni sy'n effeithio ar yr economi gyfan yn aruthrol ar hyn o bryd. Mae'r sector gofal ac iechyd yn teimlo'r pwysau hwnnw'n fwy difrifol na'r rhan fwyaf o bobl, o ystyried yr amgylchedd y maent yn gweithio ynddo, ac yn enwedig mewn lleoliad gwledig, lle mae tanwydd ar gyfer cludiant ysbyty, er enghraifft, yn elfen fawr o ddarparu'r gwasanaeth hwnnw. Yn 2022, pan gawsom y cynnydd sydyn diwethaf yng nghostau ynni, dywedodd y Gweinidog iechyd ar y pryd fod y sector iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol newydd gael bil ynni annisgwyl o dros £200 miliwn oherwydd yr argyfwng yn Wcráin. A ydych chi'n gweld y mathau hynny o ffigurau'n codi oherwydd yr argyfwng yn y gwlff, o ystyried eu bod wedi digwydd bron ar yr un adeg o'r flwyddyn, ym mis Chwefror y flwyddyn honno, ac rydym nawr yn yr hydref? Ac os yw'r pwysau ynni hwnnw'n cynyddu, ac yn costio cymaint o arian i'r sector iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol, a ydych chi'n gwneud cais i'r Gweinidog cyllid i gefnogi byrddau iechyd a darparwyr gofal cymdeithasol i dalu am y costau ynni hyn, neu a fydd disgwyl iddynt ddefnyddio eu cyllidebau fel y'u dyrannwyd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thanks for the question, and we do appreciate and understand that a lot of people, organisations and businesses across Wales will be feeling the squeeze over the coming months as energy costs increase. My officials are continuously monitoring the situation. At the moment, it doesn't look like we've got any price spikes coming through from the health sector, or demands coming through. But, as I said, we are monitoring that, and if the issue should arise, then I will be immediately dealing with the case and talking to my colleagues here in Government.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn, ac rydym yn gwerthfawrogi ac yn deall y bydd llawer o bobl, sefydliadau a busnesau ledled Cymru yn teimlo'r pwysau dros y misoedd nesaf wrth i gostau ynni gynyddu. Mae fy swyddogion yn monitro'r sefyllfa'n barhaus. Ar hyn o bryd, nid yw'n edrych fel pe bai gennym unrhyw godiadau sydyn i brisiau na galwadau wedi bod o'r sector iechyd. Ond fel y dywedais, rydym yn monitro hynny, ac os yw'r mater yn codi, byddaf yn delio â'r achos ar unwaith ac yn siarad gyda fy nghyd-Aelodau yma yn y Llywodraeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cludiant Cleifion nad yw’n Gludiant Brys
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Non-emergency Patient Transport Service

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn monitro achosion lle mae Ymddiriedolaeth GIG Gwasanaethau Ambiwlans Cymru yn canslo cludiant cleifion nad yw’n gludiant brys ar fyr rybudd yn Sir Fynwy Torfaen? OQ64614
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. How is the Welsh Government monitoring late cancellations by the Welsh Ambulance Services NHS Trust of non-emergency patient transport in Monmouthshire and Torfaen? OQ64614

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for the question. The NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee holds the Welsh Ambulance Services University NHS Trust to account through routine performance scrutiny, including cancellation trends, causes and geographical patterns. WAST’s improvement programme is strengthening reporting and action to reduce late cancellations, improve communication and provide a more reliable service for patients in Monmouthshire Torfaen and across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn. Mae Cyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru yn dwyn Ymddiriedolaeth Brifysgol GIG Gwasanaethau Ambiwlans Cymru i gyfrif drwy graffu'n gyson ar berfformiad, gan gynnwys tueddiadau canslo, achosion a phatrymau daearyddol. Mae rhaglen wella Ymddiriedolaeth Gwasanaethau Ambiwlans Cymru yn cryfhau adrodd a chamau gweithredu i leihau nifer yr achosion o ganslo'n hwyr, gwella cyfathrebu a darparu gwasanaeth mwy dibynadwy i gleifion yn Sir Fynwy Torfaen a ledled Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cabinet Minister, the Welsh ambulance service quite rightly complains that patients cancel non-emergency transport at the last minute, with it reported that 20,000 had been cancelled until July, and around 60,000 last year. However, it seems that no such monitoring happens when the service itself cancels transport. Indeed, a recent consultation on the proposed changes to the service contained this statement:

'Demand for transport continues to increase, and journeys regularly have to be cancelled because demand exceeded available capacity.' 

In other words, bookings are taken for seats that might not even exist. That's a failure of organisation and a real failure of the NHS. Very recently, a care home in my constituency was instructed that a resident would be collected earlier than planned, otherwise the transport would be cancelled. The home managed to comply, but it was stressful, and the patient arrived two hours early for her appointment and was out of the care home for over five hours. This is wholly unacceptable. Cabinet Minister, cancelled transport means wasted NHS appointment time and undue stress on patients and carers. Will you instruct your officials to establish the extent of the problem, the causes and the solutions?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Weinidog Cabinet, mae gwasanaeth ambiwlans Cymru yn cwyno, yn gywir ddigon, fod cleifion yn canslo cludiant mewn achosion nad ydynt yn rhai brys ar y funud olaf, gan nodi bod 20,000 wedi’u canslo hyd at fis Gorffennaf, ac oddeutu 60,000 y llynedd. Fodd bynnag, ymddengys nad oes unrhyw fonitro o’r fath pan fydd y gwasanaeth ei hun yn canslo cludiant. Yn wir, roedd ymgynghoriad diweddar ar y newidiadau arfaethedig i’r gwasanaeth yn cynnwys y datganiad hwn:

'Mae'r galw am drafnidiaeth yn parhau i gynyddu ac mae'n rhaid canslo teithiau'n rheolaidd oherwydd bod y galw'n fwy na'r capasiti sydd ar gael.'

Mewn geiriau eraill, mae archebion yn cael eu cymryd ar gyfer seddau nad ydynt yn bodoli hyd yn oed o bosibl. Mae hynny'n fethiant trefniadol ac yn fethiant gwirioneddol gan y GIG. Yn ddiweddar iawn, dywedwyd wrth gartref gofal yn fy etholaeth y byddai'n rhaid i breswylydd gael ei chasglu'n gynharach nag a gynlluniwyd, neu byddai'n rhaid canslo'r cludiant. Llwyddodd y cartref i gydymffurfio, ond roedd yn llawer o straen, a chyrhaeddodd y claf ddwy awr yn gynnar ar gyfer ei hapwyntiad ac roedd allan o'r cartref gofal am dros bum awr. Mae hyn yn gwbl annerbyniol. Weinidog Cabinet, mae cludiant wedi'i ganslo yn golygu gwastraffu amser apwyntiadau'r GIG, a straen gormodol ar gleifion a gofalwyr. A wnewch chi gyfarwyddo eich swyddogion i geisio deall maint y broblem, yr achosion a'r atebion?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: You're absolutely right to highlight the impact that cancellations can have on some of the most vulnerable people in our communities. Access to healthcare isn't just about the appointment itself, as you rightly say; it's also about ensuring that people can travel to and from that appointment safely and reliably. This is precisely why the NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee, and the Welsh ambulance services NHS trust have accepted the need for further improvement in non-emergency patient transport services. For many people, reliable transport is not a convenience; it's what makes access to healthcare possible. The focus of the trust's improvement programme is therefore on improving reliability, reducing avoidable cancellations, and ensuring those with the greatest need and who meet the eligibility criteria for transport are able to get to appointments and back home safely, and with dignity. This programme includes a public engagement exercise that is currently live, and I encourage service users to contribute to ensure all voices are heard.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydych chi'n llygad eich lle i dynnu sylw at yr effaith y gall canslo apwyntiadau ei chael ar rai o'r bobl fwyaf agored i niwed yn ein cymunedau. Mae a wnelo mynediad at ofal iechyd â mwy na'r apwyntiad ei hun, fel y dywedwch yn gywir ddigon; mae a wnelo hefyd â sicrhau y gall pobl deithio'n ddiogel ac yn ddibynadwy i'r apwyntiad hwnnw ac oddi yno. Dyma'n union pam y mae Cyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru, ac Ymddiriedolaeth GIG Gwasanaethau Ambiwlans Cymru wedi derbyn yr angen am welliant pellach mewn gwasanaethau cludo cleifion mewn achosion nad ydynt yn rhai brys. I lawer o bobl, nid cyfleustra yw cludiant dibynadwy; dyma sy'n gwneud mynediad at ofal iechyd yn bosibl. Felly, mae rhaglen wella'r ymddiriedolaeth yn canolbwyntio ar wella dibynadwyedd, lleihau achosion o ganslo y gellir ei osgoi, a sicrhau bod y rhai sydd â'r angen mwyaf ac sy'n bodloni'r meini prawf cymhwystra ar gyfer cludiant yn gallu cyrraedd apwyntiadau a dychwelyd adref yn ddiogel, a chydag urddas. Mae'r rhaglen hon yn cynnwys ymarfer ymgysylltu â'r cyhoedd sy'n mynd rhagddo ar hyn o bryd, ac rwy'n annog defnyddwyr gwasanaeth i gyfrannu i sicrhau bod pob llais yn cael ei glywed.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Gweinidog, getting to and from appointments using NHS-provided transport or public transport is a significant challenge in Sir Fynwy Torfaen, as we've just heard, and one that affects those who are already the most vulnerable. I've heard accounts of constituents who have been unable to secure transport home from hospitals after treatment, and even having to pay for hotels just to make early appointments. For those without enough money to pay or without supportive friends and family, appointments can be missed, and people struggling may have to pay large sums for taxis. For those less well-off, the effects are severe. So, what steps is the Government taking to make sure the most vulnerable in our society can get to and from essential appointments and treatments safely? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae mynd i apwyntiadau ac yn ôl gan ddefnyddio cludiant a ddarperir gan y GIG neu gludiant cyhoeddus yn her sylweddol yn Sir Fynwy Torfaen, fel rydym newydd ei glywed, ac yn effeithio ar y rhai sydd fwyaf agored i niwed eisoes. Rwyf wedi clywed straeon am etholwyr sydd wedi methu sicrhau cludiant adref o ysbytai ar ôl triniaeth, a hyd yn oed wedi gorfod talu am westai er mwyn cyrraedd apwyntiadau cynnar. I'r rhai nad oes ganddynt ddigon o arian i dalu, neu ffrindiau a theulu cefnogol, gallant fethu apwyntiadau, ac efallai y bydd yn rhaid i bobl sydd eisoes o dan bwysau dalu llawer o arian am dacsis. I'r rhai llai cefnog, mae'r effeithiau'n ddifrifol. Felly, pa gamau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i sicrhau y gall y rhai mwyaf agored i niwed yn ein cymdeithas fynd a dod yn ddiogel o apwyntiadau a thriniaethau hanfodol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that supplementary question, which makes a crucial point about the access to public transport and the links of public transport to our health organisations. I was at Llantrisant Health Park recently—you might have seen the new development there—and one of the first questions I asked was about access on public transport in order for people to attend appointments at the new Llantrisant Health Park once it's up and running. This applies equally to district general hospitals across Wales, and when you think about the area that you represent and the people there served by the Grange, Nevill Hall, the Royal Gwent, and, in fact, Nevill Hall serves others as well, in Powys. So, it is crucial that we get this right. That's why consideration of access to healthcare is part of the new franchising model that's being rolled out for buses here in Wales. My colleagues and I work closely with the Deputy Minister for Transport, Mark Hooper, and are discussing this regularly.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn atodol, sy'n gwneud pwynt hollbwysig ynglŷn â mynediad at drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus a chysylltiadau trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus â'n sefydliadau iechyd. Roeddwn ym Mharc Iechyd Llantrisant yn ddiweddar—efallai eich bod wedi gweld y datblygiad newydd yno—ac roedd un o'r cwestiynau cyntaf a ofynnais yn ymwneud â mynediad at drafnidiaeth gyhoeddus er mwyn i bobl fynychu apwyntiadau ym Mharc Iechyd newydd Llantrisant pan fydd yn weithredol. Mae hyn yr un mor berthnasol i ysbytai cyffredinol dosbarth ledled Cymru, a phan feddyliwch am yr ardal rydych chi'n ei chynrychioli a'r bobl yno a wasanaethir gan ysbyty'r Faenor, Nevill Hall, Ysbyty Brenhinol Gwent, ac mewn gwirionedd, mae Ysbyty Nevill Hall yn gwasanaethu eraill hefyd, ym Mhowys. Felly, mae'n hanfodol ein bod yn cael hyn yn iawn. Dyna pam y mae ystyried mynediad at ofal iechyd yn rhan o'r model masnachfreinio newydd sy'n cael ei gyflwyno ar gyfer bysiau yma yng Nghymru. Mae fy nghyd-Aelodau a minnau'n gweithio'n agos gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth, Mark Hooper, ac yn trafod hyn yn rheolaidd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Minister, you've answered many of my points, but I'll echo some of the concerns raised by Mr Senior and Mr Jones. In our community, there are many people who often feel disadvantaged because, when that important non-emergency patient transport is cancelled at short notice, it leaves a lot of vulnerable people needing to attend appointments. We've got one constituent who has to have regular trips to a doctor, can't drive, and sometimes she is let down and can't get the access to her treatment. This has incurred £100 taxi fees. Now, she has to have the treatment, but she cannot always afford, obviously, the taxi. So, how is the Welsh Government going to ensure that rural patients are not disproportionately affected by short-notice transport cancellations?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog Cabinet, rydych chi wedi ateb llawer o fy mhwyntiau, ond rwyf am adleisio rhai o'r pryderon a godwyd gan Mr Senior a Mr Jones. Yn ein cymuned ni, mae llawer o bobl sy'n aml yn teimlo dan anfantais, oherwydd pan fydd y gwasanaethau cludo cleifion mewn achosion nad ydynt yn rhai brys yn cael eu canslo ar fyr rybudd, mae'n gadael llawer o bobl agored i niwed sy'n gorfod mynychu apwyntiadau. Mae gennym un etholwr sy'n gorfod mynd i weld meddyg yn rheolaidd, ni all yrru, ac weithiau mae ei chludiant yn cael ei ganslo ac ni all gael mynediad at ei thriniaeth. Mae hyn wedi arwain at ffioedd tacsi o £100. Nawr, mae'n rhaid iddi gael y driniaeth, ond yn amlwg, ni all fforddio tacsi bob amser. Felly, sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru’n mynd i sicrhau nad yw cleifion mewn ardaloedd gwledig yn cael eu heffeithio'n anghymesur o ganlyniad i ganslo cludiant ar fyr rybudd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. You make an important point there about the fact that, if people can't access their healthcare, then they have to pay, and it's not exactly free at the point of delivery then. As I said, this is an issue where WAST is conducting a current review, and I would encourage the Member and others to contribute to the review of the non-emergency patient transport service so that we can assess the situation and improve the situation, moving forward.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Rydych chi'n gwneud pwynt pwysig yno ynglŷn â'r ffaith, os na all pobl gael mynediad at eu gofal iechyd, yna mae'n rhaid iddynt dalu, ac nid yw am ddim pryd a lle bynnag y caiff ei ddarparu bryd hynny. Fel y dywedais, mae hwn yn fater lle mae Ymddiriedolaeth Gwasanaethau Ambiwlans Cymru yn cynnal adolygiad ar hyn o bryd, a buaswn yn annog yr Aelod ac eraill i gyfrannu at yr adolygiad o'r gwasanaeth cludo cleifion mewn achosion nad ydynt yn rhai brys fel y gallwn asesu'r sefyllfa a gwella'r sefyllfa wrth symud ymlaen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Lefarwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from Party Spokespeople

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar lefarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Llefarydd Reform UK, Benjamin Hodge Mckenna.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. The Reform UK spokesperson, Benjamin Hodge Mckenna.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Minister, I was enjoying the work of the Minister for government effectiveness earlier this week by looking at the new digital dashboards. In the waiting lists section, I'm sure you'll be aware that, unfortunately, they're going in the wrong direction: total waiting lists and two-year waits are both up. Now, I acknowledge you received a terrible inheritance from Welsh Labour, but we're past the first 100 days of your Government now, we're closing in on six months, and we're heading into the winter, where we all know pressures are going to be worse. Now, originally, the First Minister said that two-year waits would be eradicated within months of a Plaid Cymru Government, and then it changed to being within a first year. So, will you take the opportunity today to commit that two-year waits will be eradicated by May of next year, or are you going to move the goalposts again on this issue?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog, roeddwn yn mwynhau gwaith y Gweinidog dros effeithiolrwydd llywodraeth yn gynharach yr wythnos hon wrth iddo edrych ar y dangosfyrddau digidol newydd. Yn yr adran restrau aros, rwy'n siŵr y byddwch yn ymwybodol, yn anffodus, eu bod yn mynd i'r cyfeiriad anghywir: mae cyfanswm y rhestrau aros a'r arosiadau dwy flynedd wedi cynyddu. Nawr, rwy'n cydnabod eich bod wedi derbyn etifeddiaeth ofnadwy gan Lafur Cymru, ond mae 100 diwrnod cyntaf eich Llywodraeth wedi mynd heibio bellach, rydym yn agosáu at chwe mis, ac rydym yn mynd i mewn i'r gaeaf, lle gŵyr pob un ohonom y bydd y pwysau'n gwaethygu. Nawr, i ddechrau, dywedodd y Prif Weinidog y byddai arosiadau dwy flynedd yn cael eu dileu o fewn misoedd i ethol Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru, ac yna newidiodd i fod o fewn y flwyddyn gyntaf. Felly, a wnewch chi achub ar y cyfle heddiw i ymrwymo y bydd arosiadau dwy flynedd yn cael eu dileu erbyn mis Mai y flwyddyn nesaf, neu a ydych chi'n mynd i symud pyst y gôl eto ar y mater hwn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thanks to the Member for giving me the opportunity to once again respond to questions around waiting lists, which I have exercised quite often over the last few months, so whatever I say won't be new. You are quite right that the numbers are going up currently. That is part of the legacy of what we are dealing with from the previous Government. So, what we did over the summer period was announce the £145 million that is going into tackling the waiting lists—£45 million in capital and £100 million of revenue funds. Then, during the recess period, we had conversations with the health boards and clinicians to draw up the plans for how that funding was going to go into the system, what the plans were going to look like. Health boards provided the final plans to me at the beginning of this month, and that's when the money started to be pumped into the system. Health boards will be paid on delivery of outcomes, not paid upfront. So, yes, while we can expect to see the waiting lists go up when they are announced again this month, for the month of August, once the money is going into the system we can expect to see those waiting lists come down. And, yes, I am confident that we will be hitting the target on the two-year waits.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i'r Aelod am roi'r cyfle imi ymateb unwaith eto i gwestiynau ynghylch rhestrau aros, rhywbeth rwyf wedi'i wneud yn eithaf aml dros yr ychydig fisoedd diwethaf, felly beth bynnag a ddywedaf, ni fydd yn newydd. Rydych chi'n llygad eich lle fod y niferoedd yn codi ar hyn o bryd. Mae hynny'n rhan o'r gwaddol rydym yn delio ag ef gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol. Felly, yr hyn a wnaethom dros gyfnod yr haf oedd cyhoeddi'r £145 miliwn, sy'n mynd tuag at fynd i'r afael â'r rhestrau aros—£45 miliwn mewn cyfalaf a £100 miliwn o gyllid refeniw. Yna, yn ystod y toriad, cawsom sgyrsiau gyda'r byrddau iechyd a chlinigwyr i lunio'r cynlluniau ar gyfer sut y byddai'r cyllid hwnnw'n mynd i mewn i'r system, sut olwg fyddai ar y cynlluniau. Darparodd y byrddau iechyd y cynlluniau terfynol i mi ddechrau'r mis, a dyna pryd y dechreuodd yr arian gael ei bwmpio i mewn i'r system. Bydd byrddau iechyd yn cael eu talu ar ôl i'r canlyniadau gael eu cyflawni, nid ymlaen llaw. Felly, er y gallwn ddisgwyl gweld y rhestrau aros yn cynyddu pan gânt eu cyhoeddi unwaith eto y mis hwn, ar gyfer mis Awst, pan fydd yr arian yn mynd i mewn i'r system, gallwn ddisgwyl gweld y rhestrau aros hynny'n lleihau. Ac ydw, rwy'n hyderus y byddwn yn cyrraedd y targed ar yr arosiadau dwy flynedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm glad to hear the commitment from you that you will be eradicating two-year waits in May. I hope I'm not going to be stood here holding you to account on that next year.

One thing that will impact waiting lists is access to GP surgeries. The number of GPs in Wales has decreased by 106 over the last few years, and the people needing treatment per GP has increased by 30 per cent. I spoke with the BMA last week, who launched the Save our Surgeries campaign. Natasha Asghar from the Welsh Conservatives launched a statement of opinion on this issue. I've supported it, alongside Reform colleagues, Welsh Labour have supported it, and the Liberal Democrats have supported it, but not a single person from Plaid Cymru has supported that statement of opinion, Minister. Why not?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n falch o glywed yr ymrwymiad gennych y byddwch yn dileu arosiadau dwy flynedd ym mis Mai. Gobeithio na fyddaf yn sefyll yma yn eich dwyn i gyfrif am hynny y flwyddyn nesaf.

Un peth a fydd yn cael effaith ar restrau aros yw mynediad at feddygfeydd teulu. Mae nifer y meddygon teulu yng Nghymru wedi gostwng 106 dros yr ychydig flynyddoedd diwethaf, ac mae nifer y bobl sydd angen triniaeth fesul meddyg teulu wedi cynyddu 30 y cant. Yr wythnos diwethaf, siaradais â Chymdeithas Feddygol Prydain, a lansiodd ymgyrch Achubwch ein Meddygfeydd. Lansiodd Natasha Asghar o'r Ceidwadwyr Cymreig ddatganiad barn ar y mater hwn. Rwyf wedi'i gefnogi, ynghyd â chyd-Aelodau o Reform, mae Llafur Cymru wedi'i gefnogi, ac mae'r Democratiaid Rhyddfrydol wedi'i gefnogi, ond nid oes unrhyw un o Blaid Cymru wedi cefnogi'r datganiad barn hwnnw, Weinidog. Pam?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Because we're taking action on this. I've spoken to the BMA several times before being in this position and since about the importance of primary care and GPs and their roles. They are crucial, you're quite right. If we are going to tackle your first question around the waiting lists, we need to get things right in the GP setting. That's why we've committed to recruiting 100 GPs before the end of this term, making sure that they are deployed to the areas where they are needed most. We have a programme where we will be supporting GPs and ensuring that we build on the current structures that we've got in order to have more co-operative models so that we can help take the back-room costs away from them and allow them to invest in the medical services that they want to provide. So, yes, I'm happy to work with the BMA and others on this. It's one of our priorities, and that's why you'll see us deliver on this and things improve by the end of our term.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Am ein bod yn gweithredu ar hyn. Rwyf wedi siarad â Chymdeithas Feddygol Prydain sawl gwaith cyn dod i'r swydd hon ac ers hynny ynglŷn â phwysigrwydd gofal sylfaenol a meddygon teulu a'u rolau. Maent yn hanfodol, rydych chi'n llygad eich lle. Os ydym am fynd i'r afael â'ch cwestiwn cyntaf ynghylch y rhestrau aros, mae angen inni gael pethau'n iawn yn y meddygfeydd teulu. Dyna pam ein bod wedi ymrwymo i recriwtio 100 o feddygon teulu cyn diwedd tymor y Senedd hon, gan sicrhau eu bod yn cael eu defnyddio yn yr ardaloedd lle mae eu hangen fwyaf. Mae gennym raglen lle byddwn yn cefnogi meddygon teulu ac yn sicrhau ein bod yn adeiladu ar y strwythurau presennol sydd gennym er mwyn cael mwy o fodelau cydweithredol fel y gallwn helpu i gael gwared ar y costau ystafell gefn a chaniatáu iddynt fuddsoddi yn y gwasanaethau meddygol y maent am eu darparu. Felly, ydw, rwy'n fwy na pharod i weithio gyda Chymdeithas Feddygol Prydain ac eraill ar hyn. Mae'n un o'n blaenoriaethau, a dyna pam y byddwch yn ein gweld yn cyflawni hyn a phethau'n gwella erbyn diwedd ein tymor.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, I don't understand why that means your party couldn't support the statement of opinion.

One area that we do agree on is the need for and use of surgical hubs in Wales. I'm glad that you mentioned Llantrisant Health Park, because that was a site that I also visited recently, alongside other MSs in the Chamber. All of the MSs who were on that visit were told very clearly that the Plaid Cymru Government will not see one spade in the ground when it comes to building any more surgical hubs, due to the planning and approval processes, within this Senedd term, let alone build the 10 that your Government is targeting. So, what are you doing to speed up that planning and approval process so that we can get on with building the health infrastructure that we desperately need here in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, nid wyf yn deall pam y mae hynny'n golygu na allai eich plaid gefnogi'r datganiad barn.

Un maes rydym yn cytuno arno yw'r angen am hybiau llawfeddygol yng Nghymru a'r defnydd ohonynt. Rwy'n falch eich bod wedi sôn am Barc Iechyd Llantrisant, gan fod hwnnw'n safle yr ymwelais ag ef yn ddiweddar, ynghyd ag ASau eraill yn y Siambr. Dywedwyd wrth yr holl ASau yn glir iawn ar yr ymweliad hwnnw na fydd Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru yn gweld yr un rhaw yn y ddaear o fewn tymor y Senedd hon o ran adeiladu unrhyw hybiau llawfeddygol pellach oherwydd y prosesau cynllunio a chymeradwyo, heb sôn am adeiladu'r 10 y mae eich Llywodraeth yn eu targedu. Felly, beth rydych chi'n ei wneud i gyflymu'r broses gynllunio a chymeradwyo honno fel y gallwn fynd ati i adeiladu'r seilwaith iechyd y mae ei angen mor daer arnom yma yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member is right; it is frustrating that the planning process can hold things up. That's why we will be working with the Minister for planning, Siân Gwenllian, here, on identifying how we can improve that planning process for essential infrastructure. But I think, more importantly, when we talk about up to 10 surgical hubs, it's not necessarily about building new ones all of the time, it's about better utilisation of the theatre spaces that we've got, utilising some of the spaces that are in the hospitals at the moment that could be used for theatre space. I was in Nevill Hall recently, and there was one theatre there that was used as a waiting room for patients. Now, that can't be right. So, you could add something on to that hospital as a waiting room and then reutilise that as a theatre space to bring down the waiting lists. So, there's a mix and match of things we can do in this space, which is what we're looking at and why we set up the expert group to identify how best we roll out those surgical hubs across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod yn llygad ei le; mae'n rhwystredig fod y broses gynllunio'n gallu arafu pethau. Dyna pam y byddwn yn gweithio gyda'r Gweinidog cynllunio, Siân Gwenllian, yma, ar nodi sut y gallwn wella'r broses gynllunio honno ar gyfer seilwaith hanfodol. Ond yn bwysicach fyth, rwy'n credu, pan fyddwn yn siarad am hyd at 10 hyb llawfeddygol, nid yw o reidrwydd yn golygu adeiladu rhai newydd drwy'r amser, mae'n golygu gwell defnydd o'r theatrau sydd gennym, gan ddefnyddio rhai o'r mannau sydd yn yr ysbytai ar hyn o bryd y gellid eu defnyddio fel theatrau. Roeddwn yn ysbyty Nevill Hall yn ddiweddar, ac roedd un theatr yno'n cael ei defnyddio fel ystafell aros i gleifion. Nawr, ni all hynny fod yn iawn. Felly, gallech ychwanegu rhywbeth at yr ysbyty hwnnw fel ystafell aros ac ailddefnyddio honno fel theatr i leihau'r rhestrau aros. Felly, mae cymysgedd o bethau y gallwn eu gwneud yn y cyswllt hwn, a dyna rydym yn edrych arno a pham y gwnaethom sefydlu'r grŵp arbenigol i nodi'r ffordd orau o gyflwyno'r hybiau llawfeddygol hynny ledled Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Ken Skates.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Ken Skates.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Minister, are there any Welsh Government whistleblowing investigations currently taking place or recently concluded relating to personnel in NHS Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog, a oes unrhyw ymchwiliadau chwythu'r chwiban yn ymwneud â phersonél yn GIG Cymru ar y gweill neu wedi'u cwblhau'n ddiweddar gan Lywodraeth Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Not that I am aware of, Ken, but if you are aware of any issues that you think should be brought to my attention then please do so.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Nid hyd y gwn i, Ken, ond os ydych chi'n ymwybodol o unrhyw faterion y credwch y dylid eu dwyn i fy sylw, gwnewch hynny ar bob cyfrif.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Minister. Over many, many years, we've been told that it's for health boards to hire and fire senior executives, yet chief executives of health boards are not accountable to their own health boards for the proper stewardship of public money or for delivering against performance requirements. Instead, accountability is to the chief executive of NHS Wales. It's also the CEO of NHS Wales who confers accountable officer status on all Welsh LHBs, and can remove it as well. That obviously leads to an awkward split in terms of accountability and responsibilities, and it no doubt creates tensions. Would you agree that it's time to devolve the responsibilities centralised in NHS Wales to local health boards, so that local control and accountability can flourish?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Dros flynyddoedd lawer, dywedwyd wrthym mai lle'r byrddau iechyd yw penodi a diswyddo uwch-swyddogion gweithredol, ond nid yw prif weithredwyr byrddau iechyd yn atebol i'w byrddau iechyd eu hunain am ddefnyddio arian cyhoeddus yn briodol neu am gyflawni yn erbyn gofynion perfformiad. Yn hytrach, maent yn atebol i brif weithredwr GIG Cymru. Prif Swyddog Gweithredol GIG Cymru sydd hefyd yn rhoi statws swyddog atebol i bob bwrdd iechyd lleol yng Nghymru, a gall ei ddileu hefyd. Mae hynny'n amlwg yn arwain at raniad lletchwith o ran atebolrwydd a chyfrifoldebau, ac mae'n sicr o greu tensiynau. A fyddech chi'n cytuno ei bod yn bryd datganoli'r cyfrifoldebau sydd wedi'u canoli yn GIG Cymru i fyrddau iechyd lleol, fel y gall rheolaeth ac atebolrwydd lleol ffynnu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: That's an interesting question, because the structure that we have around the accountability framework is a legacy of your Government, something that my predecessor, Edwina Hart, had set up originally back in 2009. I'm not happy with the current accountability framework. I don't think it allows for transparent accountability, hence why we brought in the new framework for escalation last week. I think we do need to look at the accountability structure within the NHS so that people can have confidence. The fact that, as a Minister, I can only appoint the chair of a health board means that I don't have many sticks when it comes to holding them to account. So, I'd be more than happy to look at that structure. In fact, I've asked officials to look at the accountability framework, and I'm happy to work with you, should you want to do so.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae hwnnw'n gwestiwn diddorol, gan fod y strwythur sydd gennym o amgylch y fframwaith atebolrwydd wedi'i etifeddu gan eich Llywodraeth chi, rhywbeth a sefydlwyd gan fy rhagflaenydd, Edwina Hart, yn wreiddiol yn ôl yn 2009. Nid wyf yn fodlon ar y fframwaith atebolrwydd presennol. Ni chredaf ei fod yn caniatáu atebolrwydd tryloyw, a dyna pam y gwnaethom gyflwyno'r fframwaith newydd ar gyfer uwchgyfeirio yr wythnos diwethaf. Credaf fod angen inni edrych ar y strwythur atebolrwydd o fewn y GIG fel y gall pobl gael hyder. Mae'r ffaith mai dim ond cadeirydd bwrdd iechyd y gallaf ei benodi fel Gweinidog yn golygu nad oes gennyf lawer o rym i'w dwyn i gyfrif. Felly, rwy'n fwy na pharod i edrych ar y strwythur hwnnw. Mewn gwirionedd, rwyf wedi gofyn i swyddogion edrych ar y fframwaith atebolrwydd, ac rwy'n fwy na pharod i weithio gyda chi, pe baech chi eisiau gwneud hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Natasha Asghar.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Conservatives spokesperson, Natasha Asghar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you so much, Deputy Presiding Officer. Minister, I listened to your response to the Reform Member, and, before I go into my questioning, if you want to divert your attention for surgical hubs to the Royal Gwent in Newport, you will not hear any complaints from me.

Going to my first question, I, like so many others in this Chamber, had the real misfortune, I'm afraid, of having to read through your Government's programme for government. Now, whilst it's jam-packed with ambition—no, it really was not a 'yay'—it was very light on detail, which I suppose is the Plaid Cymru way. Now, it created a lot of fanfare with catchy announcements, but it never actually explained how things were going to be delivered.

Cabinet Minister, there are nearly half a million unpaid carers in Wales who look after their loved ones day in, day out, saving the Government billions—and I mean billions—of pounds. To put it into perspective, across the UK, it would cost £185 billion every single year if the state was to replace the care provided by unpaid carers with professional paid care support. Now, despite the mammoth contribution unpaid carers make, their work often goes unnoticed, with a lack of support on offer. It is clear this Government needs to be doing a lot more when it comes to helping unpaid carers, but it doesn't look like that's happening, especially after reading your programme for government. Cabinet Minister, can you please explain to me, and this Chamber, why there were more commitments in your programme for government to Euro 2026, independence and the Tour de France than there are to improving the lives of unpaid carers in Wales? And why have unpaid carers been deprioritised by this Government? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog, gwrandewais ar eich ymateb i'r Aelod Reform, a chyn imi ddechrau gofyn fy nghwestiynau, os ydych chi eisiau dargyfeirio eich sylw i hybiau llawfeddygol a'i roi i Ysbyty Brenhinol Gwent yng Nghasnewydd, ni fyddwch yn clywed unrhyw gwynion gennyf i.

I ddod at fy nghwestiwn cyntaf, cefais i, fel cynifer o bobl eraill yn y Siambr hon, y profiad gwirioneddol annifyr, mae arnaf ofn, o orfod darllen drwy raglen lywodraethu eich Llywodraeth. Nawr, er ei bod yn llawn uchelgais—na, nid oedd yn 'hwrê' o gwbl—roedd yn brin iawn o fanylion, sef ffordd Plaid Cymru o fynd o'i chwmpas hi, mae'n debyg. Nawr, fe greodd lawer o ffanffer gyda chyhoeddiadau deniadol, ond ni wnaeth egluro sut y byddai pethau'n cael eu cyflawni.

Weinidog Cabinet, mae bron i hanner miliwn o ofalwyr di-dâl yng Nghymru sy'n gofalu am eu hanwyliaid ddydd ar ôl dydd, gan arbed biliynau—ac rwy'n golygu biliynau—o bunnoedd i'r Llywodraeth. I roi hynny mewn persbectif, ledled y DU, byddai'n costio £185 biliwn y flwyddyn pe bai'r wladwriaeth yn darparu cymorth gofal proffesiynol am dâl yn lle'r gofal a ddarperir gan ofalwyr di-dâl. Nawr, er gwaethaf y cyfraniad enfawr y mae gofalwyr di-dâl yn ei wneud, mae eu gwaith yn aml yn cael ei ddiystyru, heb ddigon o gymorth ar gael. Mae'n amlwg fod angen i'r Llywodraeth hon wneud llawer mwy i helpu gofalwyr di-dâl, ond nid yw'n edrych fel pe bai hynny'n digwydd, yn enwedig ar ôl darllen eich rhaglen lywodraethu. Weinidog Cabinet, a allwch chi egluro i mi, ac i'r Siambr hon, pam roedd mwy o ymrwymiadau yn eich rhaglen lywodraethu i Ewro 2026, annibyniaeth a'r Tour de France nag i wella bywydau gofalwyr di-dâl yng Nghymru? A pham y mae gofalwyr di-dâl wedi cael eu dadflaenoriaethu gan y Llywodraeth hon? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dirprwy Lywydd, I'd like to thank the Member for that line of questioning. Now, the programme for government is an excellent piece of work—many here would agree. But the job of the programme for government isn't to set out the absolute detail of every piece of legislation or every part of work that we'll be doing; it's to set the direction. And the same applies to the announcements that we as Ministers have made. Now, this question lies in the portfolio of my colleague the Deputy Minister. She has set out the priorities that she has in her portfolio, and she did mention and talk about the importance of unpaid carers. In fact, a lot of what we've been doing with unpaid carers is based on the brilliant report by the health committee—health and care committee, I should say—in the last Senedd, of which I was a member. And we are now actively working on those recommendations in order to ensure that unpaid carers here have the dignity and respect that they deserve. But I would suggest that you raise it with my Deputy Minister in order to push the agenda forward on this.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ddirprwy Lywydd, hoffwn ddiolch i'r Aelod am ei chwestiynau. Nawr, mae'r rhaglen lywodraethu'n ddogfen ragorol—byddai llawer yma'n cytuno. Ond nid diben y rhaglen lywodraethu yw nodi holl fanylion yr holl ddeddfwriaeth na phob rhan o'r gwaith y byddwn yn ei wneud; ei nod yw gosod y cyfeiriad. Ac mae'r un peth yn wir am y cyhoeddiadau rydym ni fel Gweinidogion wedi'u gwneud. Nawr, mae'r cwestiwn hwn ym mhortffolio fy nghyd-Aelod y Dirprwy Weinidog. Mae hi wedi nodi'r blaenoriaethau sydd ganddi yn ei phortffolio, ac fe soniodd am bwysigrwydd gofalwyr di-dâl. Mewn gwirionedd, mae llawer o'r hyn rydym wedi bod yn ei wneud gyda gofalwyr di-dâl yn seiliedig ar yr adroddiad gwych gan bwyllgor iechyd—pwyllgor iechyd a gofal, dylwn ddweud—y Senedd ddiwethaf, yr oeddwn yn aelod ohono. Ac rydym bellach yn mynd ati'n weithredol i weithio ar yr argymhellion hynny er mwyn sicrhau bod gofalwyr di-dâl yma'n cael yr urddas a'r parch y maent yn eu haeddu. Ond carwn awgrymu eich bod yn codi hyn gyda fy Nirprwy Weinidog er mwyn gwthio'r agenda ar hyn yn ei blaen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you so much. I anticipated that response from you, Cabinet Minister—surprise, surprise. And I appreciate carers do fall under the Deputy Minister's brief, but I am talking specifically about the programme for government. And, as Cabinet Minister, I'm afraid the buck stops with you on this one.

Cabinet Minister, sadly, it's not just unpaid carers who have been seemingly kicked to the kerb by your Government. The programme for government quite rightly makes specific commitments relating to cardiovascular disease, strokes, mental health and diabetes, yet it does not say anything specifically about lung disease, despite it being the third biggest killer here in Wales. Not only that, but Wales has the highest lung disease mortality rate in western Europe. Given the scale of lung disease in Wales, why has it been omitted from the Government's programme? And what message does this send to the hundreds of thousands of people living with lung conditions who continue to experience some of the worst outcomes anywhere in western Europe? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Roeddwn yn rhagweld yr ymateb hwnnw gennych, Weinidog Cabinet—dim syndod. Ac rwy'n sylweddoli bod gofalwyr yn rhan o friff y Dirprwy Weinidog, ond rwy'n sôn yn benodol am y rhaglen lywodraethu. Ac fel y Gweinidog Cabinet, mae arnaf ofn mai chi sy'n gyfrifol yn y pen draw.

Weinidog Cabinet, yn anffodus, nid gofalwyr di-dâl yn unig sydd fel pe baent wedi cael eu hanwybyddu gan eich Llywodraeth. Mae'r rhaglen lywodraethu, yn gywir ddigon, yn gwneud ymrwymiadau penodol ynghylch clefyd cardiofasgwlaidd, strôc, iechyd meddwl a diabetes, ond nid yw'n dweud unrhyw beth penodol am glefyd yr ysgyfaint, er mai dyma'r trydydd lladdwr mwyaf yma yng Nghymru. Nid yn unig hynny, ond Cymru sydd â'r gyfradd farwolaethau uchaf o glefyd yr ysgyfaint yng ngorllewin Ewrop. O ystyried pa mor gyffredin yw clefyd yr ysgyfaint yng Nghymru, pam nad oes cyfeiriad ato yn y rhaglen lywodraethu? A pha neges y mae hyn yn ei hanfon at y cannoedd o filoedd o bobl sy'n byw gyda chyflyrau'r ysgyfaint ac sy'n parhau i brofi rhai o'r canlyniadau gwaethaf yn unrhyw le yng ngorllewin Ewrop? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I think you're right, the programme for government did list a non-exhaustive list of a number of health issues that are related to people in Wales. When I say 'non-exhaustive', it means that there are others out there that we will be tackling and looking at. Lung disease is clearly one of them, and we know that, when it comes to lung cancer, it is one of the biggest killers in Wales still. That's why one of the priorities of our Government is in that preventative field, so that we stop people reaching that stage of living with or suffering from lung cancer. And that's why one of our ambitions is to roll out lung screening in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Rwy'n credu eich bod yn llygad eich lle, roedd y rhaglen lywodraethu yn cynnwys rhestr anghyflawn o nifer o faterion iechyd mewn perthynas â phobl Cymru. Pan ddywedaf 'anghyflawn', mae'n golygu bod yna rai eraill y byddwn yn mynd i'r afael â nhw ac yn edrych arnynt. Mae clefyd yr ysgyfaint yn amlwg yn un ohonynt, a gwyddom, o ran canser yr ysgyfaint, ei fod yn un o'r lladdwyr mwyaf yng Nghymru o hyd. Dyna pam mai un o flaenoriaethau ein Llywodraeth yw'r maes ataliol, fel ein bod yn atal pobl rhag cyrraedd y cam lle maent yn byw gyda chanser yr ysgyfaint neu'n dioddef ohono. A dyna pam mai un o'n huchelgeisiau yw cyflwyno rhaglen sgrinio ar gyfer yr ysgyfaint yng Nghymru.
