XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf nawr ar lafarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Yn gyntaf, llefarydd Reform UK, Francesca O'Brien.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. First, Reform UK spokesperson, Francesca O'Brien.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Cabinet Minister, I'm sorry to disappoint you by returning to a subject the Government clearly doesn't want to talk about, but the people of Wales, I believe, want answers. My office has asked all 22 Welsh councils about nationality in social housing. Last year, Cardiff Council allocated almost 30 per cent of new social housing to foreign nationals. In Newport, almost 20 per cent of social housing went to foreign nationals. Does the Welsh Government collect the nationality of people given social housing from councils, and what is the figure for Wales as a whole?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, mae'n ddrwg gennyf eich siomi drwy ddychwelyd at bwnc y mae'n amlwg nad yw'r Llywodraeth eisiau siarad amdano, ond credaf fod pobl Cymru eisiau atebion. Mae fy swyddfa wedi gofyn i bob un o'r 22 cyngor yng Nghymru am genedligrwydd mewn perthynas â thai cymdeithasol. Y llynedd, dyrannodd Cyngor Caerdydd bron i 30 y cant o dai cymdeithasol newydd i wladolion tramor. Yng Nghasnewydd, aeth bron i 20 y cant o dai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor. A yw Llywodraeth Cymru’n casglu data ar genedligrwydd pobl sy'n cael tai cymdeithasol gan gynghorau, a beth yw'r ffigur ar gyfer Cymru gyfan?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The priority of this Government is to ensure that people living here in Wales can access safe, affordable homes, and that goes for everybody living here in Wales. The allocations policy, the national allocations policy, is a framework set by the Welsh Government. The local policies then are set by the local authorities. We don't collect information within those regimes about people's nationalities. Houses are allocated according to need.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Blaenoriaeth y Llywodraeth hon yw sicrhau y gall pobl sy'n byw yma yng Nghymru gael mynediad at gartrefi diogel a fforddiadwy, ac mae hynny'n wir am bawb sy'n byw yma yng Nghymru. Mae'r polisi dyraniadau, y polisi dyraniadau cenedlaethol, yn fframwaith a osodir gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Yna, mae'r polisïau lleol yn cael eu gosod gan yr awdurdodau lleol. Nid ydym yn casglu gwybodaeth o fewn y trefniadau hynny am genedligrwydd pobl. Mae tai yn cael eu dyrannu yn ôl angen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I expected that answer, Cabinet Minister, because many councils don't hold that data either. Either they couldn't or they wouldn't tell me the truth. From Swansea to Wrexham, many of them either refused to tell us on cost grounds or, even more shockingly, they didn't collect nationality data at all. And where the housing stock has been transferred to housing associations, they aren't subject to freedom of information requests at all.

Minister, in opposition, you tabled amendments on publishing housing register data. Will you now require every council and housing association in Wales to record and publish the nationality of applicants, new tenants and households in temporary accommodation? These questions matter when our own people are waiting years for social housing—it should be for the people of this country.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Roeddwn yn disgwyl yr ateb hwnnw, Weinidog Cabinet, gan nad yw llawer o gynghorau'n cadw'r data hwnnw chwaith. Naill ai na allent neu eu bod yn gwrthod dweud y gwir wrthyf. O Abertawe i Wrecsam, gwrthododd llawer ohonynt ddweud wrthym ar sail cost, neu'n fwy syfrdanol fyth, nid oeddent yn casglu data cenedligrwydd o gwbl. A lle mae'r stoc dai wedi'i throsglwyddo i gymdeithasau tai, nid ydynt yn ddarostyngedig i geisiadau rhyddid gwybodaeth o gwbl.

Weinidog, pan oeddech chi mewn gwrthblaid, fe gyflwynoch chi welliannau ar gyhoeddi data cofrestrau tai. A fyddwch chi'n ei gwneud hi'n ofynnol nawr i bob cyngor a chymdeithas dai yng Nghymru gofnodi a chyhoeddi cenedligrwydd ymgeiswyr, tenantiaid newydd ac aelwydydd mewn llety dros dro? Mae'r cwestiynau hyn yn bwysig pan fo'n pobl ni ein hunain yn aros am flynyddoedd am dai cymdeithasol—dylent fod ar gyfer pobl y wlad hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Why do we need to collect that data? I'm not quite sure. Because everybody in Wales deserves to have a safe, affordable home, and that includes social housing as well as other forms of housing. So, I really don't see why we need to collect information around what you call 'foreign nationals'.

Now, 'foreign nationals' is a very wide-ranging term, and the vast majority of social housing tenants in Wales are UK nationals, as it happens. But, then, foreign nationals are part of our society. They're important people within our society. They're people with children. They're people working in the NHS. They're care home workers. And, of course, they are welcome here and they are contributing to our economy. I think we have very different agendas going on here, and I'm not quite sure that what you're trying to talk about is quite on the same page as I am. Absolutely, it's not on the same page.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Pam y mae angen inni gasglu'r data hwnnw? Nid wyf yn gwbl sicr. Oherwydd mae pawb yng Nghymru yn haeddu cartref diogel a fforddiadwy, ac mae hynny'n cynnwys tai cymdeithasol yn ogystal â mathau eraill o dai. Felly, nid wyf yn gweld pam y mae angen inni gasglu gwybodaeth ar yr hyn rydych chi'n eu galw'n 'wladolion tramor'.

Nawr, mae 'gwladolion tramor' yn derm eang iawn, ac mae'r mwyafrif helaeth o denantiaid tai cymdeithasol yng Nghymru yn wladolion y DU, fel y mae'n digwydd. Ond wedyn mae gwladolion tramor yn rhan o'n cymdeithas. Maent yn bobl bwysig yn ein cymdeithas. Maent yn bobl â phlant. Maent yn bobl sy'n gweithio yn y GIG. Maent yn weithwyr cartrefi gofal. Ac wrth gwrs, mae croeso iddynt yma ac maent yn cyfrannu at ein heconomi. Rwy'n credu bod gennym agendâu gwahanol iawn yma, ac nid wyf yn gwbl sicr fod yr hyn rydych chi'n ceisio siarad amdano ar yr un dudalen â'r un rwyf i arni. Yn sicr, nid yw ar yr un dudalen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, Minister, I think data matters when it's taxpayers' money, and we need to know who is in our social homes. When we've got parents waiting for years for social homes, we need to be prioritising our own. So, Minister, there are actions you can take if you wanted to fix the problem right now and put our own people first. 

Councils need both the data and the powers to act. Last December, you tabled an amendment that removed section 35 from the Homelessness and Social Housing Allocation (Wales) Bill. You said social housing was—and you have said it—a universal resource. That provision would have allowed councils to decide who does and does not qualify for social housing in their area—the same kind of power English councils use to apply residency tests. 

Will you now reintroduce that power for Welsh councils, so that social housing in Wales goes to the people of that country, and who have been waiting for years for social homes?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, Weinidog, rwy'n credu bod data'n bwysig pan ydym yn trafod arian trethdalwyr, ac mae angen inni wybod pwy sydd yn ein tai cymdeithasol. Pan fydd gennym rieni'n aros am flynyddoedd am dai cymdeithasol, mae angen inni flaenoriaethu ein pobl ein hunain. Felly, Weinidog, mae camau y gallwch eu cymryd os ydych chi eisiau datrys y broblem ar unwaith a rhoi ein pobl ein hunain yn gyntaf.

Mae angen y data a'r pwerau ar gynghorau i weithredu. Fis Rhagfyr diwethaf, cyflwynwyd gwelliant gennych a oedd yn dileu adran 35 o Fil Digartrefedd a Dyrannu Tai Cymdeithasol (Cymru). Fe ddywedoch chi fod tai cymdeithasol—ac rydych chi wedi dweud hyn—yn adnodd cyffredinol. Byddai'r ddarpariaeth honno wedi caniatáu i gynghorau benderfynu pwy sy'n gymwys a phwy nad yw'n gymwys ar gyfer tai cymdeithasol yn eu hardal—yr un math o bŵer ag y mae cynghorau Lloegr yn ei ddefnyddio i gymhwyso profion preswylio.

A wnewch chi ailgyflwyno’r pŵer hwnnw nawr i gynghorau Cymru, fel bod tai cymdeithasol yng Nghymru yn mynd i bobl y wlad hon, pobl sydd wedi bod yn aros ers blynyddoedd am dai cymdeithasol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The problem is a fundamental one. We don't have enough social housing in Wales. We don't have enough to meet the demand, to meet the need that there is—absolutely, obviously, there is not enough there available. The queue is way too long for social housing, and creating division amongst people who are in the queue, which is exactly what you are doing, is not the way forward. The way forward is to build more social homes. And that is why this Government has a relentless focus on building and creating 20,000 new social homes before the end of this Senedd term.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r broblem yn un sylfaenol. Nid oes gennym ddigon o dai cymdeithasol yng Nghymru. Nid oes gennym ddigon i ateb y galw, i ddiwallu'r angen sydd yma—yn sicr, yn amlwg, nid oes digon ar gael. Mae'r ciw am dai cymdeithasol yn llawer rhy hir, ac nid creu rhaniadau ymhlith y bobl sydd yn y ciw, sef yr hyn rydych chi'n ei wneud, yw'r ffordd ymlaen. Y ffordd ymlaen yw adeiladu mwy o dai cymdeithasol. A dyna pam y mae gan y Llywodraeth hon ffocws di-baid ar adeiladu a chreu 20,000 o dai cymdeithasol newydd cyn diwedd tymor y Senedd hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Jayne Bryant.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Jayne Bryant.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. Launched by the Welsh Labour Government in 2022, and managed by individual councils, Leasing Scheme Wales allows councils to lease properties from private landlords. It helps councils move tenants out of temporary accommodation, and tenancy support is offered as part of the scheme. An independent evaluation found that empty properties accounted for over 60 per cent of the properties within the scheme, and the evaluation also found that the co-ordination and communications established by the previous Welsh Government were highly valued by councils, and, actually, all 22 local authorities in Wales had signed up to the scheme.

However, councils and landlords are now facing uncertainty as it seems that the Plaid Cymru Welsh Government will not continue the scheme beyond March next year, with no new properties onboarded after December this year. So, Cabinet Minister, can you provide clarity on the future of this scheme to councils, landlords and tenants, and what will replace Leasing Scheme Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Wedi'i lansio gan Lywodraeth Lafur Cymru yn 2022, a'i reoli gan gynghorau unigol, mae Cynllun Lesio Cymru yn caniatáu i gynghorau lesio eiddo gan landlordiaid preifat. Mae'n helpu cynghorau i symud tenantiaid allan o lety dros dro, a chynigir cymorth tenantiaeth fel rhan o'r cynllun. Canfu gwerthusiad annibynnol fod dros 60 y cant o'r eiddo sy'n rhan o'r cynllun yn wag, a chanfu'r gwerthusiad hefyd fod y cynghorau'n werthfawrogol iawn o'r cydgysylltu a'r cyfathrebu a sefydlwyd gan Lywodraeth flaenorol Cymru, ac mewn gwirionedd, roedd pob un o'r 22 awdurdod lleol yng Nghymru wedi ymuno â'r cynllun.

Fodd bynnag, mae cynghorau a landlordiaid bellach yn wynebu ansicrwydd gan ei bod yn ymddangos na fydd Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru yn parhau â'r cynllun y tu hwnt i fis Mawrth y flwyddyn nesaf, heb unrhyw eiddo newydd yn cael eu cofrestru ar ôl mis Rhagfyr eleni. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, a allwch chi roi eglurder ynghylch dyfodol y cynllun hwn i gynghorau, landlordiaid a thenantiaid, a beth a ddaw yn lle Cynllun Lesio Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn am y cwestiwn. A dwi’n cofio pan ddaeth y cynllun yma i mewn, ac, ar y pryd, roedd o’n cael ei ddisgrifio fel cynllun pum mlynedd a oedd efo pwrpas penodol o fedru dod â mwy o dai i fyny i safon fel eu bod nhw’n gallu cael eu defnyddio i helpu efo’r sefyllfa ddigartrefedd.

Mae’r cynllun i ddod i ben yn fuan, ond mae’r eiddo sydd o fewn y cynllun yna’n barod a’r ceisiadau sydd o fewn y pipeline yna yn dal i fodoli. Y gwir amdani ydy bod y cynllun yna wedi dod â phwrpas iddo fo, ac o fewn y cyfyngiadau ariannol y mae’r Llywodraeth yma’n eu hwynebu, mae o’n un o’r pethau dŷn ni’n edrych arno fo o ddifrif rŵan, ynglŷn â dyfodol y cynllun.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much for that question. And I do recall when this plan was introduced, and, at the time, it was described as a five-year programme that had a specific purpose of bringing more houses up to standard so that they could be used to alleviate homelessness. 

The scheme is to come to an end soon, but the properties that are within the scheme already and the applications in that pipeline will still exist. The truth is that that scheme had a particular purpose, and within the financial restrictions that this Government is facing, it is one of the things we are looking at now in earnest, in terms of the scheme's future.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Cabinet Minister. I'd recommend you do look at that scheme because, as I said, the feedback from many was how effective it had been, particularly for reluctant landlords.

Whilst every town and city centre has its own unique identity, many are facing the similar challenge of changing footfall and empty properties. That's why the Welsh Labour Government's Transforming Towns programme boosted regeneration in town and city centres across Wales, with more than £300 million since 2020. Instead of confirming a continuation of this programme, Cabinet Minister, you've created a town-centre taskforce, and I've no doubt that the two co-chairs and 17 members announced last week have vast expertise. But I'd like to know what the Government expects of the taskforce and what it expects to deliver. How will the taskforce differ from previous reviews and recommendations, when will it report and how much will it cost to convene the town-centre taskforce?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Buaswn yn argymell eich bod yn edrych ar y cynllun hwnnw, oherwydd fel y dywedais, roedd yr adborth gan lawer yn dangos pa mor effeithiol y bu, yn enwedig i landlordiaid amharod.

Er bod gan ganol pob tref a dinas ei hunaniaeth unigryw ei hun, mae llawer yn wynebu her debyg o ran y newid yn nifer yr ymwelwyr ac eiddo gwag. Dyna pam y rhoddodd rhaglen Trawsnewid Trefi Llywodraeth Lafur Cymru hwb i adfywio canol trefi a dinasoedd ledled Cymru, gyda mwy na £300 miliwn ers 2020. Yn hytrach na chadarnhau parhad y rhaglen hon, Weinidog Cabinet, rydych chi wedi creu tasglu canol trefi, ac nid oes gennyf unrhyw amheuaeth fod gan y ddau gyd-gadeirydd a'r 17 aelod a gyhoeddwyd yr wythnos diwethaf arbenigedd helaeth. Ond hoffwn wybod beth y mae'r Llywodraeth yn ei ddisgwyl gan y tasglu a beth y mae'n disgwyl ei gyflawni. Sut y bydd y tasglu'n wahanol i adolygiadau ac argymhellion blaenorol, pryd y bydd yn adrodd a faint y mae'n mynd i'w gostio i gynnull y tasglu canol trefi?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn am y cwestiwn yna. Fel mae'n digwydd, dwi'n mynd i fod yn cyhoeddi yfory gyllid ychwanegol ar gyfer nifer o drefi, ac un ddinas, yng Nghymru o dan gyllid Transforming Towns. Felly, mae'r cyllid yna wedi bod yn fodd arbennig o effeithiol o fedru caniatáu i drefi a dinasoedd wella canol eu trefi.

Ar hyn o bryd, dŷn ni wedi, fel dŷch chi'n gwybod, sefydlu'r tasglu sydd yn edrych ar bob agwedd o'r hyn sydd angen ei wneud wrth inni ailddychmygu canol ein trefi. Roeddech chi'n gofyn beth fydd cwmpas gwaith y tasglu. Bydd y tasglu yn edrych ar bopeth, yn mynd ar draws ffiniau traddodiadol, efallai, ond yn dod â phopeth at ei gilydd, o ran cynllunio, o ran trethi busnes, o ran canfod cyfalaf ychwanegol—yr holl faterion yna.

Mae'r tasglu wedi cyfarfod. Mi wnes i fynd atyn nhw ar ddechrau eu cyfarfod nhw yr wythnos diwethaf. Yr adborth dwi wedi ei gael o'r cyfarfod yna ydy eu bod nhw wedi bod wrthi drwy'r dydd yn adnabod y themâu pwysig yma sydd angen eu rhoi ar waith. Fy neges i ar ddechrau eu cyfarfod nhw oedd hyn: dwi ddim eisiau i chi ddisgrifio'r broblem i fi, dwi ishio ichi ddod â datrysiadau. Dwi ishio ichi ddod ag argymhellion clir ymlaen o beth fedrwn ni ei wneud fel Llywodraeth yng Nghymru. Mae rhai materion—yn ymwneud efo'r economi ac ati—y tu hwnt i'n gallu ymarferol ni yn fan hyn. Felly, roeddwn i'n rhoi'r pwyslais yn glir ar beth fedrwn ni ei wneud yng Nghymru i wella'r ffordd y mae canol ein trefi ni'n datblygu ac i roi bywyd newydd iddyn nhw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much for that question. As it happens, I will be announcing additional funding tomorrow for a number of towns, and one city, in Wales under the Transforming Towns funding. So, that funding has been a very effective means of allowing towns and cities to improve their town centres.

At the moment, as you know, we have established a taskforce, which is looking at all aspects of what needs to be done as we reimagine our town centres. You were asking what the purpose of the taskforce will be. It will look at everything, across traditional boundaries, perhaps, but will draw everything together, in terms of planning, in terms of business rates, in terms of finding additional capital—all of those issues.

The taskforce has met. I joined them at the beginning of their meeting last week. The feedback that I've had from that meeting was that they had been working all day identifying these important themes that need to be addressed. My message at the beginning of their meeting was this: I don't want you to describe the problem to me, I want you to find solutions. I want clear recommendations in terms of what we as a Government in Wales can do. There are certain issues—related to the economy and so on—that are beyond our practical powers here. So, I placed a clear emphasis on what we in Wales can do in order to improve the way that our town centres develop and to give them new life.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Peter Fox.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Conservatives' spokesperson, Peter Fox.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Llywydd. Cabinet Minister, Wales continues to face significant housing pressures. We hear it all the time in this Chamber: rising homelessness, growing demand for affordable homes. Now, at the Conservative conference this week, which I'm sure you were following, the shadow chancellor announced some excellent proposals, aimed at reducing the costs of building new homes and reforming planning rules to support housing delivery.

Cabinet Minister, does the Welsh Government accept that planning delays, bureaucracy and developer contribution requirements can act as a barrier to delivering the homes Wales needs? In England, the Conservatives want to replace section 106 agreements as they are a real barrier for developers. Will you review Wales's approach and, in a similar way, bring forward changes where planning requirements are preventing or delaying the delivery of much-needed affordable and social housing?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, mae Cymru’n parhau i wynebu pwysau sylweddol o ran tai. Rydym yn clywed hynny drwy'r amser yn y Siambr hon: digartrefedd cynyddol, galw cynyddol am dai fforddiadwy. Nawr, yng nghynhadledd y Ceidwadwyr yr wythnos hon, y byddwch chi wedi bod yn ei dilyn, rwy'n siŵr, cyhoeddodd canghellor yr wrthblaid gynigion rhagorol, gyda'r nod o leihau costau adeiladu tai newydd a diwygio rheolau cynllunio i gefnogi'r ddarpariaeth dai.

Weinidog Cabinet, a yw Llywodraeth Cymru yn derbyn y gall oedi yn y broses gynllunio, biwrocratiaeth a gofynion cyfraniadau datblygwyr weithredu fel rhwystr i'r gwaith o ddarparu'r cartrefi sydd eu hangen ar Gymru? Yn Lloegr, mae'r Ceidwadwyr eisiau cael gwared ar gytundebau adran 106 gan eu bod yn rhwystr gwirioneddol i ddatblygwyr. A wnewch chi adolygu dull Cymru o weithredu, a chyflwyno newidiadau mewn ffordd debyg lle mae gofynion cynllunio'n atal neu'n gohirio'r ddarpariaeth o dai fforddiadwy a chymdeithasol y mae eu hangen yn fawr?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch am y cwestiwn. Yn ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni, fe welwch chi fod yna ymrwymiad yn y fan yna i ddiwygio'r system gynllunio, i wneud y system gynllunio yn fwy atebol i gymunedau, a hefyd i weld sut y medrwn ni gyflymu'r broses o ganiatâd cynllunio a thynnu rhai o'r rhwystrau oddi yno. Felly, mae cynllunio yn faes allweddol, a dŷn ni'n cydnabod bod ganddo fo rôl allweddol o ran cyflawni nifer o bolisïau eraill—tai yn enwedig.

Ond hefyd, mae cynllunio yn medru ein helpu ni i fynd i'r afael â gwrthdaro rhwng polisïau, lle mae'n codi. Felly, dwi'n grediniol fod angen i ni roi sylw penodol i hyn. Dwi wedi cyhoeddi yr wythnos diwethaf ein bod ni'n ymgynghori ar y fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol. O dan hwnna mae 'Polisi Cynllunio Cymru' yn gorwedd. Mi fyddaf i hefyd yn gwneud galwad am dystiolaeth o gwmpas sut y medrwn ni'n wirioneddol symud ymlaen efo'r hyn rydyn ni'n cytuno efo'n gilydd arno fo, sef yr angen i ddiwygio ymhellach y system gynllunio. Mi fyddwn i wrth fy modd petaech chi yn dod â rhai o'ch syniadau ymlaen, o gwmpas 106, yn sicr, ond am faterion eraill hefyd. Dwi'n annog pawb yn y Siambr yma sydd efo syniadau ar sut i wneud y system yn fwy atebol i ddod â syniadau ymlaen.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you for the question. In our programme for government, you will see that there is a clear commitment there to reform the planning system, to make the planning system more accountable to communities, and also to see how we can accelerate the process of providing planning consents and removing some of the barriers from the system. So, planning is a key area, and we recognise that it has a key role in delivering many other policies, particularly in the field of housing.

But planning can also assist us in tackling conflict between policies, where those issues arise. Therefore, I am convinced that we need to give particular attention to this. I did announce last week that we would be consulting on the national development framework. 'Planning Policy Wales' sits under that. I will also be making a call for evidence around how we can make meaningful progress with what we all agree on, namely the need to further reform the planning system. I would be delighted if you were to bring some of your own ideas forward, around 106 issues, certainly, but on other issues too. I encourage everyone in this Chamber who has ideas as to how we can make the system more accountable to bring their ideas forward.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for that, Cabinet Minister. That's reassuring, and I'll be very pleased to contribute some of our ideas. Clearly, if planning is a blocker to delivering the houses we need, we need to level some of those barriers.

Moving on to a different subject that you're responsible for, Cabinet Minister, and that's the Welsh fire service. They have continued to promote the Wales Wildfire Board's Burn to Protect campaign. Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service and North Wales Fire and Rescue Service have both highlighted the need for preventative action following the horrific scenes we saw all through the summer. Recent scrutiny by Audit Wales has highlighted wider concerns around the financial sustainability of our fire service and the costs associated with improved programmes. Given the increasing threat posed by extreme weather conditions, what assessment have you made of whether Wales's fire and rescue services have sufficient resources and funding to respond to increasing wildfire incidents, particularly in south Wales, following the severe wildfire season we've just experienced?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Mae hynny'n galonogol, ac rwy'n fwy na pharod i gyfrannu rhai o'n syniadau. Yn amlwg, os yw cynllunio'n rhwystr i ddarparu'r tai sydd eu hangen arnom, mae angen inni gael gwared â rhai o'r rhwystrau hynny.

Os caf symud ymlaen at bwnc gwahanol rydych chi'n gyfrifol amdano, Weinidog Cabinet, sef gwasanaeth tân Cymru. Maent wedi parhau i hyrwyddo ymgyrch Bwrdd Tanau Gwyllt Cymru, Llosgi i Amddiffyn. Mae Gwasanaeth Tân ac Achub Canolbarth a Gorllewin Cymru a Gwasanaeth Tân ac Achub Gogledd Cymru wedi tynnu sylw at yr angen am gamau ataliol yn dilyn y golygfeydd erchyll a welsom drwy gydol yr haf. Mae gwaith craffu diweddar gan Archwilio Cymru wedi tynnu sylw at bryderon ehangach ynghylch cynaliadwyedd ariannol ein gwasanaeth tân a'r costau sy'n gysylltiedig â rhaglenni gwell. O ystyried bygythiad cynyddol amodau tywydd eithafol, pa asesiad a wnaethoch i weld a oes gan wasanaethau tân ac achub Cymru ddigon o adnoddau a chyllid i ymateb i danau gwyllt cynyddol, yn enwedig yn y de, yn dilyn y tymor tanau gwyllt difrifol rydym newydd ei brofi?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch i chi am y cwestiwn. Dwi am gymryd y cyfle i ddiolch unwaith eto i'n diffoddwyr tân ni, i'r heddlu, Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, cymunedau a'r asiantaethau i gyd a wnaeth weithio mor, mor galed yn ystod y tanau gwyllt dros yr haf. Cefais i gyfle i fynd yn uniongyrchol i sefyllfa anodd iawn, iawn a gweld y diffoddwyr tân wrthi mewn amgylchiadau anodd iawn yn ceisio diffodd y fflamau.

Rydych chi'n hollol iawn, mae'r gwaith ataliol sydd yn digwydd drwy'r gwasanaethau tân ac achub yn holl, holl bwysig. Maen nhw'n mynd i mewn i'n hysgolion ni ac mae ganddyn nhw wasanaeth cymunedol. Nid Llywodraeth Cymru sy'n ariannu'r gwasanaeth tân ac achub, wrth gwrs. Jest i'ch atgoffa chi, ar 22 Hydref, bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn cynnal uwchgynhadledd, summit, am y tanau gwyllt. Bydd y Prif Weinidog yn cadeirio hwnnw ac mi fyddaf i a'r Gweinidogion eraill a fuodd ynghlwm wrth yr holl danau gwyllt dros yr haf yn rhan o'r summit yna. Yn sicr, mae yna themâu pwysig i'w trafod yn sgil y tanau a ddigwyddodd. Mae angen cynllunio yn ofalus ar gyfer y ffordd ymlaen, gan gynnwys y ffordd ymlaen ar gyfer y gwasanaethau tân ac achub. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much for that question. I would like to take this opportunity to once again thank our firefighters, the police force, NRW, our communities and all of the agencies that worked so very hard during those wildfires over the summer months. I had an opportunity to go directly to a very difficult situation and saw the firefighters working in very difficult circumstances to try to extinguish those flames.

You're entirely right that the preventative work that happens through the fire and rescue services is crucially important. They go into our schools and they have a community service. The Welsh Government doesn't fund the fire and rescue service, of course. Just to remind you, on 22 October, the Welsh Government will hold a summit on wildfires. The First Minister will chair that event, and I and other Ministers who were involved with the whole issue of wildfires over the summer will be part of that summit. Certainly, there are important themes to discuss in light of the fires that did happen over the summer. We need to plan carefully for the future, including a way forward for the fire and rescue services. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. We'll move ahead now, but, before we do, can I just point out we're over two thirds of the way through the allocated time for this and yet we're only now moving to a spokesperson's question? So, if the Minister could help with short answers on this.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Rydym am symud ymlaen nawr, ond cyn inni wneud hynny, a gaf i nodi ein bod dros ddwy ran o dair o'r ffordd drwy'r amser a neilltuwyd ar gyfer hyn, ac eto dim ond nawr rydym yn symud at gwestiwn gan lefarydd? Felly, os gall y Gweinidog helpu gydag atebion byr ar hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi wedi ymrwymo i ymgysylltu'n fwy effeithlon â'r gymuned am y broses cynlluniau datblygu lleol. Mi fyddaf i’n dechrau sgwrs cyn hir ar sut i ailddychmygu cynlluniau datblygu lleol fel eu bod nhw'n adlewyrchu dyheadau ein cymunedau'n well. Fe fydd ymgynghoriad ar opsiynau a chynigion ar gyfer newid yn dilyn maes o law.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I am committed to engaging more efficiently with the community regarding the LDP process. I will be starting a conversation soon on how LDPs can be reimagined to better reflect the aspirations of our communities. A consultation on options and proposals for change will follow in due course.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn. In December 2023, Wrexham councillors were forced, under threat of imprisonment, to vote for a local development plan that was not fit for purpose. The plan was based on population projections that were spectacularly wrong. Following a lengthy court battle, brought by councillors, including me, against the previous Welsh Government and housing developers, the High Court quashed the council's decision to adopt its LDP. To cut a long story short, to suit the Llywydd, the LDP has now been withdrawn and the council is preparing a new plan. As a former councillor, I want to improve the planning system throughout Wales by ensuring greater community engagement and involvement in the process. To test that, will the Minister consider Wrexham as a pilot scheme to ensure that the local voice is heard loud and clear in the planning process, and that we never again see local elected representatives threatened with jail for standing up for their communities? Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr. Ym mis Rhagfyr 2023, gorfodwyd cynghorwyr Wrecsam, dan fygythiad o garchar, i bleidleisio dros gynllun datblygu lleol nad oedd yn addas i’r diben. Roedd y cynllun yn seiliedig ar ragolygon poblogaeth a oedd yn gwbl anghywir. Yn dilyn brwydr gyfreithiol hir, a gychwynnwyd gan gynghorwyr, gan fy nghynnwys i, yn erbyn Llywodraeth flaenorol Cymru a datblygwyr tai, diddymodd yr Uchel Lys benderfyniad y cyngor i fabwysiadu ei gynllun datblygu lleol. I dorri stori hir yn fyr, i fodloni'r Llywydd, mae'r CDLl bellach wedi'i ddiddymu ac mae'r cyngor yn paratoi cynllun newydd. Fel cyn-gynghorydd, hoffwn wella'r system gynllunio ledled Cymru drwy sicrhau mwy o ymgysylltiad a chyfranogiad cymunedol yn y broses. I brofi hynny, a wnaiff y Gweinidog ystyried Wrecsam fel cynllun peilot i sicrhau bod y llais lleol yn cael ei glywed yn glir yn y broses gynllunio, ac na fyddwn ni byth eto'n gweld cynrychiolwyr etholedig lleol yn cael eu bygwth â charchar am sefyll dros eu cymunedau? Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Marc, ac i Carrie Harper sy'n eistedd drws nesaf i chi. Dwi'n gwybod am y gwaith pwysig wnaethoch chi ei wneud yn ystod yn cyfnod yna, a ddylai neb, byth eto, fod yn wynebu carchar ac yn wynebu'r math yna o sefyllfa am fod yn llais i ddemocratiaeth yn lleol. Felly, dwi'n gobeithio eich bod chi'n cymryd hynny a bod pawb yn deall pwysigrwydd y neges yna.

Mae hi'n bwysig, wrth i'r LDP newydd gael ei chreu, bod gwersi o'r profiad blaenorol yn cael eu dysgu, gan adeiladu ar yr hyn wnaeth weithio ac yn edrych yn benodol ynglŷn â beth wnaeth ddim gweithio fel bod y plan newydd yn ennyn mwy o gefnogaeth a mwy o hyder ymhlith y cymunedau, ac yn rhoi sylfaen gref ar gyfer dyfodol Wrecsam.

Gan fod gen i bwerau o fewn y broses LDP, fedraf i ddim cymryd rhan uniongyrchol yn y broses o ddatblygu'r cynllun newydd yma, ond dwi'n hapus i roi cefnogaeth ymarferol i'r broses yna, a buaswn i'n hapus iawn i gyfarfod efo chi i glywed sut ydych chi'n meddwl y gall yr ymgysylltu cymunedol yna weithio. Mae'r Design Commission for Wales hefyd yn gallu bod o gymorth, ac mi fyddaf i'n cyfarfod efo nhw yr wythnos nesaf, felly mae'n siŵr bod yna syniadau yn fanna hefyd y gallwn ni eu cymryd i fyny.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I thank you, Marc, and Carrie Harper who is sitting alongside you. I know about the important work that you did in that period, and no-one should ever again face jail or that kind of situation for being a voice for local democracy. I hope that that is accepted and that everybody understands the importance of that message.

It is important, as the new LDP is put together, that lessons from that previous experience are learned, building on what did work and looking specifically at what didn't work so that the new plan does gain more support and confidence in the communities and provides a firm foundation for the future of Wrexham.

Given that I have powers within the LDP process, I can't take a direct role in the process of developing the new plan, but I am content to provide practical support for that process, and I would be very happy to meet with you to hear about how you think the community engagement should work. The Design Commission for Wales can also be of assistance, and I will be meeting them next week, and so there will probably be ideas there that we can explore.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, if community engagement is to mean anything, residents in communities across Flint and Wrexham must see their local voices genuinely reflected on the ground. I want to take what Sarah Edwards, my colleague, said a little bit further. So, will the Minister ensure that locally prepared place plans and town plans are given full weight in the planning process and that area-wide infrastructure improvements, such as road networks, GP capacity and school places, are fully costed and funded before large-scale housing is approved? I just want to give an example of a place in my area where there is huge development, which is Oakenholt, where there are lots of houses being built, but the GP capacity is really under pressure because of that. It was something that my colleague Ben Hodge McKenna mentioned before. So, furthermore, does the Minister agree that, where vital local infrastructure cannot be guaranteed, local planning authorities should have the backing of the Welsh Government to refuse applications? Diolch, Lywydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, os yw ymgysylltiad cymunedol yn mynd i olygu unrhyw beth, rhaid i drigolion mewn cymunedau ledled y Fflint a Wrecsam weld eu lleisiau lleol yn cael eu hadlewyrchu'n iawn ar lawr gwlad. Rwyf am fynd â'r hyn a ddywedodd Sarah Edwards, fy nghyd-Aelod, ychydig ymhellach. Felly, a wnaiff y Gweinidog sicrhau bod cynlluniau bro a chynlluniau tref a baratowyd yn lleol yn cael eu hystyried yn llawn yn y broses gynllunio a bod gwelliannau seilwaith ar draws yr ardal gyfan, fel rhwydweithiau ffyrdd, capasiti meddygfeydd teulu a lleoedd ysgol, yn cael eu prisio a'u hariannu'n llawn cyn cymeradwyo datblygiadau tai ar raddfa fawr? Rwyf am roi enghraifft o le yn fy ardal i lle mae datblygiad enfawr ar y gweill, sef Oakenholt, lle mae llawer o dai'n cael eu hadeiladu, ond mae capasiti'r meddygfeydd teulu o dan bwysau mawr oherwydd hynny. Roedd yn rhywbeth y soniodd fy nghyd-Aelod Ben Hodge McKenna amdano yn gynt. Felly, ar ben hynny, a yw'r Gweinidog yn cytuno, lle na ellir gwarantu seilwaith lleol hanfodol, y dylai awdurdodau cynllunio lleol gael cefnogaeth Llywodraeth Cymru i wrthod ceisiadau? Diolch, Lywydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, I'll reiterate what I said earlier, really, that the infrastructure absolutely needs to be at the heart of the planning process and in bringing LDPs together. They are a matter for the local councils, but my message is quite clear and the message in 'Planning Policy Wales' is quite clear that infrastructure around any housing developments, et cetera, have to meet that need as well.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, rwyf am ailadrodd yr hyn a ddywedais yn gynharach mewn gwirionedd, fod angen i'r seilwaith fod wrth wraidd y broses gynllunio ac wrth ddod â chynlluniau datblygu lleol at ei gilydd. Maent yn fater i'r cynghorau lleol, ond mae fy neges yn eithaf clir ac mae'r neges yn 'Polisi Cynllunio Cymru' hefyd yn eithaf clir fod yn rhaid i'r seilwaith o amgylch unrhyw ddatblygiadau tai ac ati ddiwallu'r angen hwnnw hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'll try and be brief. Minister, you'll be aware that Cardiff Council is delivering one of the UK's most ambitious and award-winning council house building schemes. A key factor in achieving that was having an LDP in place that enabled the council to secure greater social housing contributions from large-scale developments. Without a plan in place, Cardiff would have lost control of the process and seen piecemeal developments dispersed across the city. Too often, though, engagement on LDPs is dominated by well-organised voices opposed to development. So, Minister, in your rethinking of LDPs, how will you ensure that the voices of those on housing waiting lists, those living in temporary accommodation who desperately need social housing, are also heard, given they are far less likely to participate in these consultations compared with well-resourced, well-organised groups who don't want to see any houses built?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe geisiaf fod yn gryno. Weinidog, fe fyddwch yn ymwybodol fod un o gynlluniau adeiladu tai cyngor mwyaf uchelgeisiol ac arobryn y DU ar waith gan Gyngor Caerdydd. Un ffactor allweddol wrth gyflawni hynny oedd cael CDLl ar waith a oedd yn galluogi'r cyngor i sicrhau mwy o gyfraniadau tai cymdeithasol o ddatblygiadau mawr. Heb gynllun ar waith, byddai Caerdydd wedi colli rheolaeth ar y broses ac wedi gweld datblygiadau tameidiog yn cael eu gwasgaru ledled y ddinas. Yn rhy aml, fodd bynnag, mae'r broses ymgysylltu ar gynlluniau datblygu lleol yn cael ei llywio gan leisiau trefnedig sy'n gwrthwynebu datblygu. Felly, Weinidog, wrth ailystyried cynlluniau datblygu lleol, sut y byddwch chi'n sicrhau bod lleisiau'r rhai sydd ar restrau aros am dai, y rhai sy'n byw mewn llety dros dro ac y mae taer angen tai cymdeithasol arnynt, hefyd yn cael eu clywed, o ystyried eu bod yn llawer llai tebygol o gymryd rhan yn yr ymgynghoriadau hyn o gymharu â grwpiau trefnedig sydd â digon o adnoddau nad ydynt am i unrhyw dai gael eu hadeiladu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Yes, your point is well made, Huw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr. Mae eich pwynt wedi'i wneud yn dda, Huw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn. Mae hi'n bwysig bod y broses o greu cynllun lleol yn cynnwys pawb, onid ydy, ac anghenion pawb o fewn y gymdeithas yna. O brofiad personol, o fod yn rhan o ddatblygu cynllun datblygu lleol yn fy mhentref i, roedd y broses o ymgysylltu efo'r gymuned gyfan a dangos i'r gymuned gyfan fod yna anghenion tai, er enghraifft, yn y gymuned honno, roedd hynny'n sicrhau bod gennym ni gynllun a oedd yn gadarn ar gyfer y dyfodol. A phan ddaeth cynlluniau tai ymlaen a oedd yn rhai cymesur—ac, wrth gwrs, dyna ydy'r broblem, onid e, dydyn nhw ddim bob tro yn gymesur—ond pan oedd cynlluniau yn dod ymlaen oedd yn gymesur efo maint y pentref ond hefyd efo'r angen lleol, doedd yna ddim cwyno amdano fo. Felly, dwi'n meddwl ei bod hi'n bwysig cynnwys pawb, gan gynnwys y lleisiau hynny sydd ddim yn cael eu clywed. Rydw i'n meddwl bod gennym ni fel cynghorwyr lleol le i arwain a bod yn llais i'r anghenion yna sydd yn aml yn cael eu hanghofio.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. It is important that the process of creating a local plan does include everyone, isn't it, and the needs of everyone within that community. From my personal experience of being part of the development of a local development plan in my village, the process of engaging with the entire community and showing the entire community that there were housing needs, for example, within that community, that ensured that we did have a plan that was robust for the future, and when housing plans were brought forward that were proportionate—and, of course, that's the problem, isn't it, that they're not always proportionate—but when plans were brought forward that were proportionate in relation to the size of the village but also in relation to local need, there were no complaints about them. So, I do think it's important to include everyone, including those voices that are not heard, and I think we as local councillors have a role in leading and being a voice for those needs that are often forgotten.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I refer Members to my declaration of interest. In the programme for government, Minister, there is a piece that talks of the Government looking at examining the permitted development rights and bringing into beneficial use redundant farm buildings for housing purposes. When councils are developing development plans, they require clear guidance from central Government so that those plans can be enacted and deliver the houses that many local communities are desperate to have. If that measure was introduced, that would have a big impact on freeing up redundant buildings for beneficial purposes and creating properties that people could live in in rural settings. It's already been enacted in many parts of the United Kingdom. When will the Welsh Government be giving that guidance to councils to bring forward those properties to be redeveloped out of redundant buildings that exist in the countryside?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Cyfeiriaf yr Aelodau at fy natganiad o fuddiant. Yn y rhaglen lywodraethu, Weinidog, mae darn sy'n sôn am y Llywodraeth yn edrych ar archwilio'r hawliau datblygu a ganiateir a defnyddio adeiladau fferm diangen mewn ffordd fuddiol at ddibenion tai. Pan fydd cynghorau'n datblygu cynlluniau datblygu, mae angen canllawiau clir arnynt gan y Llywodraeth ganolog fel y gellir rhoi'r cynlluniau hynny ar waith a darparu'r tai y mae eu hangen yn fawr ar lawer o gymunedau lleol. Pe bai'r mesur hwnnw'n cael ei gyflwyno, byddai'n cael effaith fawr ar ryddhau adeiladau diangen at ddibenion buddiol a chreu eiddo y gallai pobl fyw ynddynt mewn lleoliadau gwledig. Mae hyn eisoes wedi'i ddeddfu mewn sawl rhan o'r Deyrnas Unedig. Pryd y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru’n rhoi'r cyfarwyddyd hwnnw i gynghorau ailddatblygu'r adeiladau diangen sy'n bodoli yng nghefn gwlad?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, I agree with your ambition for creating a more robust and resilient rurality here in Wales. I am in active discussions with Llyr Gruffydd, the rural affairs Minister—whatever the title is now—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, rwy'n cytuno â'ch uchelgais i greu cefn gwlad mwy cadarn a gwydn yma yng Nghymru. Rwy'n cael trafodaethau gweithredol gyda Llyr Gruffydd, y Gweinidog materion gwledig—beth bynnag yw'r teitl nawr—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: —and we are looking at this and are in active discussions around it.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa gynnydd y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i wneud o ran ei chynlluniau i amddiffyn hawliau rhentwyr? OQ64622
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What progress has the Welsh Government made on its plans to protect renters' rights? OQ64622

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae cryfhau hawliau tenantiaid yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth yma. Mae rhentwyr yn haeddu cartref diogel, cynnes a fforddiadwy, ac fe ddylen nhw deimlo'n hyderus yn herio amodau gwael. Mae newid cadarnhaol yn gofyn am gyfraith dda, a bydd cam cyntaf ein rhaglen ddeddfwriaethol yn amddiffyn tenantiaid yn well, yn mynd i'r afael â landlordiaid gwael ac yn gwneud rhentu yn fwy diogel.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Strengthening tenants' rights is a priority for this Government. Renters deserve a safe, warm, secure and affordable home, and they should feel confident challenging poor conditions. Positive change requires good law, and the first phase of our legislative programme will better protect tenants, tackle poor landlords and make renting more secure.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Minister. Strengthening the rights and protection for renters is, as you know, fundamental for ending the housing emergency in Wales. The Government's response so far does not meet the scale of the challenge. We are approaching another winter where people will be living in cold, freezing, damp, inadequate homes, and this is already a crisis. Families in Wales are spending over a third of their income on rent in the private sector, and they are still subject to the risk of a no-fault eviction, something that has been outlawed in England and Scotland but not in Wales. People across Wales need reassurance that you will stand up for their rights and protect them from unscrupulous landlords. Will you commit to ending no-fault evictions at the earliest possible opportunity, and will you now commit to an immediate freezing of rents in the private rental sector to give people much needed breathing space in the cost-of-living crisis? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Mae cryfhau hawliau ac amddiffyniadau i rentwyr, fel y gwyddoch, yn hanfodol ar gyfer dod â'r argyfwng tai yng Nghymru i ben. Nid yw ymateb y Llywodraeth hyd yn hyn yn cyfateb i faint yr her. Rydym yn agosáu at aeaf arall lle bydd pobl yn byw mewn cartrefi oer, rhewllyd, llaith ac annigonol, ac mae hyn eisoes yn argyfwng. Mae teuluoedd yng Nghymru yn gwario dros draean o'u hincwm ar rent yn y sector preifat, ac maent yn dal i fod mewn perygl o gael eu troi allan heb fai, rhywbeth sydd wedi'i wahardd yn Lloegr a'r Alban ond nid yng Nghymru. Mae angen sicrwydd ar bobl ledled Cymru y byddwch chi'n sefyll dros eu hawliau ac yn eu diogelu rhag landlordiaid diegwyddor. A wnewch chi ymrwymo i wahardd troi allan heb fai cyn gynted â phosibl, ac a wnewch chi ymrwymo nawr i rewi rhenti ar unwaith yn y sector rhentu preifat er mwyn rhoi'r lle i anadlu y mae pobl gymaint o'i angen yn ystod yr argyfwng costau byw? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am y cwestiynau yna. Mae'r sector rhentu preifat yn chwarae rhan hanfodol yn ein system dai ni, efo tua un rhan o chwech o aelwydydd yn rhentu, ac felly mae hi'n bwysig iawn ein bod ni'n rhoi sylw penodol i bobl sydd yn wynebu costau cynyddol yn y rhent ac felly yn eu costau byw. Mi ydym ni, fel Llywodraeth, yn bwriadu gwneud hyn fesul cam. Fe fyddwch chi'n sylweddoli mai Llywodraeth leiafrifol ydym ni, ac felly efallai fydd yr uchelgais yr ydych chi a fi yn ei rannu ddim yn mynd i fod yn bosib yn llwyr, ond dwi'n benderfynol o wella amodau ar gyfer rhentwyr. Y Bil rhentwyr cyntaf fydd y cam cyntaf mewn rhaglen fydd yn datblygu wrth i ni symud ymlaen. Mi fydd y Bil rhentwyr cyntaf yn ein galluogi ni i gasglu'r data angenrheidiol sydd ei angen ar gyfer gweld beth yn union ydy'r sefyllfa rhentu ar draws Cymru mewn gwahanol ardaloedd. Bydd hwnna wedyn yn rhoi sylfaen i ni adeiladu arni ar gyfer ail a thrydydd Bil. A'r nod yn y pen draw, wrth gwrs, ydy ein bod ni'n rhoi mewn cyfraith yng Nghymru yr hawl i gartref digonol, a bod hwnna'n rhan bwysig o gyfraith a deddfwriaeth yng Nghymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for those questions. The private rental sector does play a crucial role in our housing system, with around one in six households renting, and therefore it is hugely important that we give particular attention to those people who are facing increasing costs in their rent and thus in their costs of living. We, as a Government, intend to do this via a phased approach. You will realise that we are a minority Government, and so perhaps the ambition that you and I share won't be able to be delivered in full, but I am determined to improve the position for renters. The first renters Bill will be the first phase in a programme that will develop as we proceed. The first renters Bill will enable us to gather the necessary data that we need in order to see exactly what the situation in terms of renting in Wales in different areas. And that will provide us with a foundation to build on for a second and third Bill. And the aim ultimately, of course, is that we place in law in Wales the right to an adequate home, and that that is an important part of the Welsh legislative landscape.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae gofynion ansawdd datblygu Cymru yn sicrhau bod cartrefi cymdeithasol newydd yn darparu amgylchedd lle gall aelwydydd ffynnu, ac sy'n addasu i'w hanghenion newidiol. Mae gennym ni gyflenwad cryf o dai sy'n bodloni'r safonau yma, gan ddarparu cartrefi sy'n gynaliadwy, yn fforddiadwy i'w rhedeg, gan helpu i greu cymunedau bywiog ledled Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh development quality requirements ensure that new social homes provide an environment where households can thrive, and which adapt to their changing needs. We have a strong pipeline of housing that meets these standards, delivering homes that are sustainable and affordable to run, while helping to create vibrant communities across Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Over the summer, I had the opportunity to meet with Trivallis, who are undertaking a development in Penrhys, in the Rhondda, to deliver around 1,000 new homes over the next 10 years. They raised with me some challenges presented by the current development quality requirements. Trivallis has relayed to me that the current development quality requirements require housing associations to build to standards above those set by building regulations, including achieving energy performance certificate A or an alternative approved design. In Penrhys, I've been told that this is adding around 15 per cent to construction costs and achieving the required standard can be technically challenging for high-rise developments and other homes in urban areas. I'd be keen to hear your view on this, Cabinet Minister, particularly around whether we are striking the right balance between ensuring high-quality, energy-efficient homes and cost-effectiveness. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Dros yr haf, cefais gyfle i gyfarfod â Trivallis, sy'n cyflawni datblygiad ym Mhenrhys, yn y Rhondda, i ddarparu tua 1,000 o gartrefi newydd dros y 10 mlynedd nesaf. Fe wnaethant ddweud wrthyf am rai o'r heriau sy'n deillio o'r gofynion ansawdd datblygu presennol. Roedd Trivallis yn dweud bod y gofynion ansawdd datblygu presennol yn ei gwneud yn ofynnol i gymdeithasau tai adeiladu i safonau uwch na'r rhai a osodir gan reoliadau adeiladu, gan gynnwys cyflawni tystysgrif perfformiad ynni A neu gynllun amgen cymeradwy. Ym Mhenrhys, dywedwyd wrthyf fod hyn yn ychwanegu tua 15 y cant at gostau adeiladu a gall cyflawni'r safon angenrheidiol fod yn heriol yn dechnegol ar gyfer datblygiadau adeiladau uchel iawn a chartrefi eraill mewn ardaloedd trefol. Rwy'n awyddus i glywed eich barn ar hyn, Weinidog Cabinet, yn enwedig ynglŷn ag a ydym yn taro'r cydbwysedd cywir rhwng sicrhau cartrefi o ansawdd uchel, effeithlon o ran eu defnydd o ynni, a chosteffeithiolrwydd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. I have heard other social landlords cite this as something that we need to look at, and that they think that maybe the balance should be redressed a little bit. So, my officials are available to discuss any challenges Trivallis or other social landlords are facing in bringing forward proposals. I've asked my officials to look specifically at the issue raised around EPC A, and so I hope to see that work come forward in the near future.

On high-rise developments, we are pragmatic that, as long as all attempts to comply with the standard are taken, we'll accept schemes that achieve below EPC A—for instance, high EPC B with good levels of airtightness.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr. Rwyf wedi clywed landlordiaid cymdeithasol eraill yn cyfeirio at hyn fel rhywbeth y mae angen inni edrych arno, a'u bod yn meddwl efallai y dylid unioni'r cydbwysedd ychydig. Felly, mae fy swyddogion ar gael i drafod unrhyw heriau y mae Trivallis neu landlordiaid cymdeithasol eraill yn eu hwynebu wrth gyflwyno cynigion. Rwyf wedi gofyn i fy swyddogion edrych yn benodol ar y mater a godwyd ynghylch EPC A, ac felly rwy'n gobeithio gweld y gwaith hwnnw'n cael ei gyflwyno yn y dyfodol agos.

Ar ddatblygiadau adeiladau uchel iawn, rydym yn bragmatig, cyn belled â bod pob ymdrech i gydymffurfio â'r safon, byddwn yn derbyn cynlluniau sy'n cyflawni islaw EPC A—er enghraifft, EPC B uchel gyda lefelau da o aerglosrwydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Mae'r polisi cynllunio yn nodi bod angen i awdurdodau cynllunio lleol gefnogi'r gwaith o ddarparu pob math o seilwaith sydd ei angen i ddiwallu anghenion cymunedau pan fydd datblygiadau tai newydd yn cael eu hystyried.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. Planning policy sets out that local planning authorities should support the provision of all types of infrastructure required to meet the needs of communities when new housing developments are considered.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Minister, most communities in my constituency are already stretched to the limit. It's already hard to get a GP appointment, seeing an NHS dentist is almost impossible, and schools already have too many children in the classroom without the right support, yet more homes are being approved without the infrastructure there to support them.

We all want to see more housing as soon as possible, as has been said today, but there has to be some common sense attached to it. I know this has been brought up quite a number of times today in this Senedd, and I want to just reiterate points made by the Member for Carmarthenshire and the Member for Fflint Wrecsam, because my constituency shares those same pressures, and that's why I welcome the consultation that is open right now. But how do you envisage better infrastructure planning around new housing developments? And, as you develop the new national development framework following the consultation, will you work with local authorities to look to reform planning policy to ensure that any large housing developments are only approved where there is the necessary infrastructure already in place, or there is clear funding commitment to deliver it alongside the housing? As you've said today, that should be happening, but as you know and I know and this Chamber knows—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Weinidog, mae'r rhan fwyaf o gymunedau yn fy etholaeth eisoes wedi'u hymestyn i'r eithaf. Mae eisoes yn anodd cael apwyntiad meddyg teulu, mae gweld deintydd y GIG bron yn amhosibl, ac mae gan ysgolion ormod o blant yn yr ystafell ddosbarth heb y gefnogaeth gywir, eto i gyd mae mwy o gartrefi'n cael eu cymeradwyo heb y seilwaith yno i'w cefnogi.

Rydym i gyd eisiau gweld mwy o dai cyn gynted â phosibl, fel y dywedwyd heddiw, ond rhaid bod rhywfaint o synnwyr cyffredin ynghlwm wrth hynny. Rwy'n gwybod bod hyn wedi codi sawl gwaith heddiw yn y Senedd, ac rwyf am ailadrodd pwyntiau a wnaed gan yr Aelod dros Sir Gaerfyrddin a'r Aelod dros Fflint Wrecsam, oherwydd mae fy etholaeth yn rhannu'r un pwysau, a dyna pam rwy'n croesawu'r ymgynghoriad sydd ar y gweill ar hyn o bryd. Ond sut ydych chi'n rhagweld gwell cynllunio seilwaith o amgylch datblygiadau tai newydd? Ac wrth i chi ddatblygu'r fframwaith datblygu cenedlaethol newydd yn dilyn yr ymgynghoriad, a wnewch chi weithio gydag awdurdodau lleol i edrych ar ddiwygio polisi cynllunio i sicrhau bod unrhyw ddatblygiadau tai mawr ond yn cael eu cymeradwyo lle mae'r seilwaith angenrheidiol eisoes yn ei le, neu fod ymrwymiad cyllido clir i'w gyflawni ochr yn ochr â'r tai? Fel y dywedoch chi heddiw, dylai hynny fod yn digwydd, ond fel y gwyddoch chi a minnau a'r Siambr hon—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Fel rydych chi'n dweud, mi ddylai hynna fod yn digwydd, a dwi yn cyd-fynd efo lot o'r hyn roeddech chi'n ei ddweud ar hyn. Mi ddylai awdurdodau cynllunio, ar y cyd â darparwyr allweddol, gymryd agwedd strategol a hirdymor tuag at ddarparu seilwaith wrth lunio cynlluniau. Gall hynny, wrth gwrs, gynnwys cydweithio rhwng awdurdodau lleol a darparwyr seilwaith allweddol i sicrhau bod hwnnw'n gynaliadwy ac yn addas i ddiben. Felly, mae fy neges i'n glir, ond, wrth gwrs, gwaith yr awdurdodau lleol ydy creu'r cynlluniau datblygu lleol. Dwi yn meddwl y dylai pob un ohonom ni gymryd llawer mwy o sylw pan fo'r cynlluniau datblygu lleol yma yn cael eu creu, ac yn cymryd rhan yn y broses fel Aelodau o'r Senedd, fel cynghorwyr, fel cynghorwyr cymuned, fel ein bod ni, ein llais ni, ynglŷn â seilwaith ac ynglŷn â materion eraill, yn cael ei glywed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: As you say, that should be happening, and I agree with a lot of what you said on this subject. Planning authorities, along with key providers, should take a strategic and long-term approach towards providing infrastructure in drawing up plans. That can, of course, include collaboration between local authorities and key infrastructure providers to ensure that that is sustainable and fit for purpose. So, my message is clear, but, of course, it is for the local authorities to create the LDPs. I do think that all of us should take a lot more notice when those LDPs are created and should take part in the process as Members of the Senedd, as councillors and as community councillors, so that our voice, on infrastructure and other issues, is heard.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Mae Cyngor Abertawe wedi cael dros £38 miliwn o'r grant tai cymdeithasol a £9.5 miliwn drwy raglen gyfalaf llety trosiannol eleni yn unig. Efo'i gilydd, bydd hynna yn cyfrannu at ddarparu 541 o gartrefi ychwanegol ar draws y tymor seneddol hwn.

Together, this will contribute to the delivery of 541 additional homes across this Senedd term.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Minister. Minister, your Government promised 20,000 additional social homes by 2030, despite Wales's nation of sanctuary and Swansea's city of sanctuary status potentially drawing further claimants into our lands, and you just said that we do not have enough social housing. My understanding is that Swansea Council does not collect immigration status data for social housing applicants. I consider that remiss. I was also surprised that you said that you were not sure why we would collect that data. The people of Swansea and Wales deserve transparency to understand the full scale of the situation. Will your Government take concrete action to close this unacceptable void in the data and publish clear comparisons of social housing allocations and waiting times for established local residents versus newly arrived people and how crucial allocation decisions are made?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Weinidog, fe addawodd eich Llywodraeth 20,000 o gartrefi cymdeithasol ychwanegol erbyn 2030, er bod cenedl noddfa Cymru a statws dinas noddfa Abertawe o bosibl yn denu hawlwyr pellach i'n gwlad, ac fe wnaethoch chi ddweud nawr nad oes gennym ddigon o dai cymdeithasol. Fy nealltwriaeth i yw nad yw Cyngor Abertawe'n casglu data statws mewnfudo ar gyfer ymgeiswyr am dai cymdeithasol. Rwy'n ystyried hynny'n esgeulus. Roeddwn yn synnu hefyd eich bod wedi dweud nad oeddech chi'n siŵr pam y byddem yn casglu'r data hwnnw. Mae pobl Abertawe a Chymru'n haeddu tryloywder i ddeall graddfa lawn y sefyllfa. A wnaiff eich Llywodraeth roi cymryd camau pendant ar waith i gau'r bwlch annerbyniol hwn yn y data a chyhoeddi cymariaethau clir o ddyraniadau tai cymdeithasol ac amseroedd aros i drigolion lleol sefydledig yn hytrach na phobl sydd newydd gyrraedd a sut y caiff penderfyniadau dyrannu allweddol eu gwneud?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi jest yn mynd i ddweud unwaith eto fod tai cymdeithasol yn cael eu dyrannu yn ôl angen, ddim yn ôl cenedligrwydd. Pan ydych chi'n defnyddio y term 'foreign nationals', dwi ddim yn siŵr yn union beth rydych chi'n cyfeirio ato fo yn fanna. Mae 'foreign nationals' yn cynnwys pobl, teuluoedd, plant, sydd yn gweithio yn ein NHS ni, sydd yn gweithio yn ein cartrefi gofal ni, sydd yn dreifio'n bysys ni, sydd yn gwneud gwaith arbennig, gwaith pwysig sydd angen ei gyflawni yma yng Nghymru. Mae eu hanghenion nhw ar gyfer tai cymdeithasol yn cael eu hystyried yn union yr un fath ag anghenion pawb arall. Mae pawb sydd yn byw yng Nghymru yn haeddu cael cartref digonol, waeth beth ydy eu cenedligrwydd nhw, waeth beth fo'u cefndir nhw neu waeth beth fo'u rhywedd nhw. Mae pawb sydd yn byw yng Nghymru yn haeddu cael tŷ cymdeithasol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I will just repeat once again that social housing is allocated according to need, not according to nationality. When you use the term 'foreign nationals', I'm not exactly sure what you're referring to there. 'Foreign nationals' include people, families, children, who work in our NHS, who work in our care homes, who drive our buses, who do excellent and important work that needs to be done here in Wales. Their needs for social housing are considered in the same way as everyone else's needs. Everyone who lives in Wales deserves to have an adequate home, whatever their nationality, whatever their background or their sex. Everyone living in Wales deserves a home.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Mae yna dipyn o ddiddordeb yn hyn heddiw. Rhaid i’n system gynllunio ni weithredu mewn modd amserol, ond rhaid iddi hefyd, wrth gwrs, wneud penderfyniadau cadarn i gyflawni ein huchelgeisiau ni ar gyfer Cymru, yn arbennig o ran yr economi a chymunedau. Dyna pam mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni yn ein hymrwymo ni i ddiwygio’r system gynllunio.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. There is significant interest in this today. Our planning system must operate in a timely fashion, but it must also, of course, make robust decisions to deliver our ambitions for Wales, especially in terms of the economy and communities. That is why our programme for government has committed us to reform the planning system.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, people in Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr have been asking me how many more years will communities and businesses have to wait for a planning system that delivers decisions promptly. Will you commit to clear, measurable targets for reducing delays? Will you introduce clear planning performance targets for councils and Welsh Government, and publish the results so that the public can hold both to account for the delays? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae pobl ym Mhontypridd Cynon Merthyr wedi bod yn gofyn i mi faint o flynyddoedd eto y bydd yn rhaid i gymunedau a busnesau aros am system gynllunio sy'n darparu penderfyniadau'n brydlon. A wnewch chi ymrwymo i dargedau clir, mesuradwy ar gyfer lleihau oedi? A wnewch chi gyflwyno targedau perfformiad cynllunio clir ar gyfer cynghorau a Llywodraeth Cymru, a chyhoeddi'r canlyniadau fel y gall y cyhoedd ddwyn cynghorau a'r Llywodraeth i gyfrif am yr oedi? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I don't think it's quite as simple as you point out. There are delays in the system, but there are all kinds of reasons why these delays come about. I absolutely want to hear your views in the call for evidence that we are holding, some of which you've talked about now, but there are lots of other matters that can be taken into account to try and make the system more streamlined. But I do give a caution: the capacity within the planning authorities has dwindled. It's become smaller and smaller because of austerity, because of cuts that have happened where councils have had to try and protect education, social services. Quite often, it's the planning and the planners that are affected. So, please can we bear that in mind as well when we're talking about streamlining of the planning process?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Nid wyf yn credu ei fod mor syml â'r hyn a nodwch. Mae oedi yn y system, ond mae pob math o resymau dros oedi o'r fath. Rwy'n sicr yn awyddus i glywed eich safbwyntiau yn yr alwad am dystiolaeth a gynhelir gennym, ac rydych chi wedi siarad am rai ohonynt nawr, ond mae yna lawer o faterion eraill y gellir eu hystyried i geisio gwneud y system yn symlach. Ond rwy'n rhoi rhybudd: mae'r capasiti o fewn yr awdurdodau cynllunio wedi lleihau. Mae wedi mynd yn llai ac yn llai oherwydd cyni, oherwydd toriadau sydd wedi digwydd lle mae cynghorau wedi gorfod ceisio diogelu addysg, gwasanaethau cymdeithasol. Yn aml, y cynllunio a'r cynllunwyr sy'n cael eu heffeithio. Felly, a gawn ni gadw hynny mewn cof hefyd pan fyddwn yn siarad am symleiddio'r broses gynllunio?
