XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. Foreign nationals living in Welsh and British social housing should be given a grace period of three months to find private housing, after which, they should be deported. It isn't the responsibility of the Welsh or British taxpayer to fund the living arrangements of people from overseas. People moving to the UK should be able to afford to buy or rent a house at normal market rates before they move here. If they can't afford to live here without help from the taxpayer, then they shouldn't come to the UK.

Now, Kiera Marshall is right, there is a shortage of social housing in this country, but Reform would build tens of thousands more. But those homes should go to British—[Interruption.] No, thank you. Those homes should go to British people. There is no point in building thousands of new homes when net immigration is bringing in hundreds of thousands of people every year to fill them.

The British state and the Welsh state do not exist to provide social housing to the rest of the world, they exist to serve the interests of the British and Welsh people, and putting the people of Britain and Wales first necessarily means putting the rest of the world second. It isn't racist or xenophobic or unkind to regard your countrymen as your priority. Those closest to you get preferential treatment. And as a Welsh politician representing Wales, that is right, that is just and that is normal. [Interruption.] No, thank you. [Interruption.] [Laughter.]

I'm sure that was a very funny joke. Thank you. If you ask me to choose between my countrymen, the people of Wales, who are my first and only priority, and strangers, every time, I will proudly choose my countrymen. The people of Wales deserve to be a priority in their own country. They are a unique and special people with a shared history that goes back thousands of years. If, like some of my colleagues, you want to move here and join us, you are more than welcome, but you cannot require the taxpayer to fund your lifestyle.

I cannot even fathom—. I cannot even fathom the entitlement required to look at a country with failing—[Interruption.] No. I cannot even fathom the entitlement required to look at a country with failing public services, patients dying in hospital corridors, and think yourself entitled to subsidised housing when you aren't even from there. If I moved to China or Eritrea or Bangladesh and told them to house me, they would flatly tell me 'no'. They are right to do so, and we should do the same. I do not accept for a moment that it's the moral responsibility of the poorest nation in the UK to give up its social housing for people that aren't even from the UK.

Once foreign nationals have been banned from social housing, and those who cannot or will not find private accommodation are deported, the allocation system should be overhauled. It should prioritise British workers under the age of 35, young married couples, veterans, victims of domestic violence and care leavers. Being in work should also be a requirement to access any newly built social housing. These measures would go some way to reflect the fact that we live in a world of finite resources and that our own come first. So, I'll be voting in favour of the motion.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Dylid rhoi cyfnod gras o dri mis i ddinasyddion tramor sy'n byw mewn tai cymdeithasol yng Nghymru a Phrydain i ddod o hyd i dai preifat, ac ar ôl hynny, dylid eu hallgludo. Nid cyfrifoldeb y trethdalwr Cymreig neu Brydeinig yw ariannu trefniadau byw pobl o dramor. Dylai pobl sy'n symud i'r DU allu fforddio prynu neu rentu tŷ ar gyfraddau arferol y farchnad cyn iddynt symud yma. Os na allant fforddio byw yma heb gymorth gan y trethdalwr, ni ddylent ddod i'r DU.

Nawr, mae Kiera Marshall yn iawn, mae prinder tai cymdeithasol yn y wlad hon, ond byddai Reform yn adeiladu degau o filoedd yn fwy. Ond dylai'r cartrefi hynny fynd i bobl Prydain—[Torri ar draws.] Na, dim diolch. Dylai'r cartrefi hynny fynd i bobl Prydain. Nid oes pwynt adeiladu miloedd o gartrefi newydd pan fo mewnfudo net yn dod â channoedd o filoedd o bobl i mewn bob blwyddyn i'w llenwi.

Nid yw'r wladwriaeth Brydeinig a'r wladwriaeth Gymreig yn bodoli i ddarparu tai cymdeithasol i weddill y byd, maent yn bodoli i wasanaethu buddiannau pobl Prydain a Chymru, ac mae rhoi pobl Prydain a Chymru yn gyntaf o reidrwydd yn golygu rhoi gweddill y byd yn ail. Nid yw'n hiliol nac yn senoffobaidd nac yn annheg i roi blaenoriaeth i'ch cydwladwyr. Mae'r rhai agosaf atoch yn cael triniaeth ffafriol. Ac fel gwleidydd Cymreig sy'n cynrychioli Cymru, mae hynny'n iawn, mae hynny'n gyfiawn ac mae hynny'n normal. [Torri ar draws.] Na, dim diolch. [Torri ar draws.] [Chwerthin.]

Rwy'n siŵr bod honno'n jôc ddoniol iawn. Diolch. Os gofynnwch imi ddewis rhwng fy nghydwladwyr, pobl Cymru, fy mhrif flaenoriaeth a fy unig flaenoriaeth, a dieithriaid, byddaf bob tro'n falch o ddewis fy nghydwladwyr. Mae pobl Cymru'n haeddu bod yn flaenoriaeth yn eu gwlad eu hunain. Maent yn bobl unigryw ac arbennig gyda hanes cyffredin sy'n mynd yn ôl filoedd o flynyddoedd. Os ydych chi, fel rhai o fy nghyd-Aelodau, eisiau symud yma ac ymuno â ni, mae croeso mawr i chi wneud hynny, ond ni allwch ei gwneud yn ofynnol i'r trethdalwr ariannu eich ffordd o fyw.

Ni allaf hyd yn oed ddeall—. Ni allaf hyd yn oed ddeall yr ymdeimlad o hawl sydd ei angen i edrych ar wlad sy'n—[Torri ar draws.] Na. Ni allaf hyd yn oed ddeall yr ymdeimlad o hawl sydd ei angen i edrych ar wlad y mae ei gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yn methu, cleifion sy'n marw yng nghoridorau ysbytai, a meddwl bod gennych hawl i dai a gymorthdelir pan nad ydych chi'n dod o'r fan honno hyd yn oed. Pe bawn i'n symud i China neu Eritrea neu Bangladesh ac yn dweud wrthynt roi cartref i mi, byddent yn dweud 'na' ar ei ben wrthyf. Maent yn iawn i wneud hynny, a dylem ninnau wneud yr un peth. Nid wyf yn derbyn am eiliad ei bod yn gyfrifoldeb moesol ar genedl dlotaf y DU i ildio ei thai cymdeithasol i bobl nad ydynt yn dod o'r DU.

Pan fydd gwladolion tramor wedi'u gwahardd rhag cael tai cymdeithasol, a'r rhai nad ydynt yn gallu neu'n barod i ddod o hyd i lety preifat yn cael eu hallgludo, dylid ailwampio'r system ddyrannu. Dylai flaenoriaethu gweithwyr Prydeinig o dan 35 oed, cyplau priod ifanc, cyn-filwyr, dioddefwyr trais domestig a phobl sy'n gadael gofal. Hefyd, dylai fod yn ofynnol i ymgeiswyr fod mewn gwaith i gael mynediad at unrhyw dai cymdeithasol a adeiladir o'r newydd. Byddai'r mesurau hyn yn mynd rywfaint o'r ffordd i adlewyrchu'r ffaith ein bod yn byw mewn byd o adnoddau cyfyngedig a bod ein pobl ein hunain yn dod yn gyntaf. Felly, fe fyddaf i'n pleidleisio o blaid y cynnig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Homes are the foundations of our entire lives, from health and well-being to education and jobs. This motion is divisive and misleading, and it's important to put the facts front and centre of this debate.

I'll start with houses in multiple occupation. HMOs play a crucial role for university students, single individuals, people on low incomes, people who arrive to a new area, for whatever reason, or people who only want short-term housing as an option. The most recent Welsh Government data accounts for under 15,000 HMOs in Wales. A mixture of types of accommodation within communities is important, and the concentration of HMOs in certain areas is something that warrants further action. But that is a separate issue to the misleading motion that's being debated today.

The proposals put forward today to restrict the rights of people who live here legally would mean evicting workers, carers, colleagues and friends. That's the reality. If today's motion passes, this Senedd would be pitting neighbour against neighbour. It would not represent Wales and Welsh values. The evidence shows that the vast majority—94 per cent—of social housing tenants in Wales were born in the UK, and nearly 80 per cent were born in Wales. Out of almost 0.5 million residents living in social housing in Wales, 463,000 were born in the UK. Of those who are not British citizens, there are people with settled status, refugees who have been granted protection, people granted humanitarian protection, and people with a lawful immigration status, which gives them that entitlement. It's clear that social housing should continue to be allocated according to housing need and in line with legal obligations.

We know that there is pressure on local services, including housing, across communities in Wales—nobody is denying that. But the way of alleviating that pressure is to invest in public services, grow our economy, build more homes and deliver effectively across Government, not to rip up legal rights and deny people the services that they're entitled to.

Social housing in Wales is allocated based on housing need, and there are strict rules that determine eligibility. That means most people subject to immigration control aren't eligible for social housing. That is a fact, but one that some people in this Chamber refuse to recognise. There is significant disinformation and misinformation when it comes to social housing and the wider debate about immigration in Wales. It's important to emphasise that social housing allocations primarily work to serve the people of Wales. The reality is that local authorities across Wales apply tight controls around eligibility, and there's always a need to follow the correct process to ensure that housing needs are properly assessed.

Housing associations also play an increasingly important role in supporting people and communities, helping residents sustain their tenancies, improve their well-being, and access opportunities that enable them to thrive. As a result, social landlords are balancing the need to build more homes, invest in existing homes, and deliver services that respond to wider social and economic challenges. This requires strong investment, long-term investment and a shared commitment to addressing Wales's housing needs. The biggest challenge facing the housing system in Wales isn't the eligibility criteria but the need to invest in more social homes.

In the last Senedd term, the Welsh Labour Government invested £2 billion to deliver more than 20,000 homes for rent in the social sector, and that was record levels of investment and record levels of delivery. I'd like to know how the current Government is going to maintain that momentum and increase the supply of social housing across Wales, reducing the social housing waiting list. The focus of the Welsh Government should be on building more homes, bringing empty properties back into use, and making sure councils and housing associations can develop plans to increase the supply of social housing. That is what this Senedd should focus on and scrutinise.

Finally, Cabinet Minister, fear is being stoked in this Chamber today, so what is this Government doing to challenge the disinformation and misinformation around social housing eligibility? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Cartrefi yw sylfeini ein bywydau cyfan, o iechyd a lles i addysg a swyddi. Mae'r cynnig hwn yn ymrannol ac yn gamarweiniol, ac mae'n bwysig rhoi lle blaenllaw i'r ffeithiau yn y ddadl hon.

Fe ddechreuaf gyda thai aml feddiannaeth. Mae tai amlfeddiannaeth yn chwarae rôl hanfodol i fyfyrwyr prifysgol, unigolion sengl, pobl ar incwm isel, pobl sy'n cyrraedd ardal newydd am ba reswm bynnag, neu bobl sydd ond eisiau tai tymor byr fel opsiwn. Mae data diweddaraf Llywodraeth Cymru yn nodi bod llai na 15,000 o dai amlfeddiannaeth yng Nghymru. Mae cymysgedd o fathau o lety mewn cymunedau yn bwysig, ac mae crynodiad tai amlfeddiannaeth mewn rhai ardaloedd yn rhywbeth sy'n galw am weithredu pellach. Ond mae hwnnw'n fater gwahanol i'r cynnig camarweiniol sy'n cael ei drafod heddiw.

Byddai'r cynigion a gyflwynwyd heddiw i gyfyngu ar hawliau pobl sy'n byw yma yn gyfreithlon yn golygu troi gweithwyr, gofalwyr, cydweithwyr a ffrindiau allan. Dyna'r realiti. Os bydd y cynnig heddiw yn pasio, byddai'r Senedd hon yn gosod cymydog yn erbyn cymydog. Ni fyddai'n cynrychioli Cymru a gwerthoedd Cymreig. Mae'r dystiolaeth yn dangos bod y mwyafrif helaeth—94 y cant—o denantiaid tai cymdeithasol yng Nghymru wedi'u geni yn y DU, a bron i 80 y cant wedi'u geni yng Nghymru. O'r ychydig dan 0.5 miliwn o drigolion sy'n byw mewn tai cymdeithasol yng Nghymru, cafodd 463,000 eu geni yn y DU. O'r rhai nad ydynt yn ddinasyddion Prydeinig, mae yna bobl â statws preswylwyr sefydlog, ffoaduriaid y caniatawyd diogelwch iddynt, pobl y caniatawyd diogelwch dyngarol iddynt, a phobl â statws mewnfudo cyfreithlon, sy'n rhoi'r hawl honno iddynt. Mae'n amlwg y dylai tai cymdeithasol barhau i gael eu dyrannu yn ôl yr angen o ran tai ac yn unol â rhwymedigaethau cyfreithiol.

Gwyddom fod pwysau ar wasanaethau lleol, gan gynnwys tai, ar draws y cymunedau yng Nghymru—nid oes neb yn gwadu hynny. Ond y ffordd o leddfu'r pwysau hwnnw yw buddsoddi mewn gwasanaethau cyhoeddus, tyfu ein heconomi, adeiladu mwy o gartrefi a chyflawni'n effeithiol ar draws y Llywodraeth, nid chwalu hawliau cyfreithiol ac amddifadu pobl o'r gwasanaethau y mae ganddynt hawl iddynt.

Mae tai cymdeithasol yng Nghymru yn cael eu dyrannu'n seiliedig ar angen o ran tai, ac fe geir rheolau llym sy'n pennu cymhwystra. Mae hynny'n golygu nad yw'r rhan fwyaf o bobl sy'n destun rheolaeth mewnfudo yn gymwys i gael tai cymdeithasol. Mae hynny'n ffaith, ond un y mae rhai pobl yn y Siambr hon yn gwrthod ei chydnabod. Mae yna ddiffyg gwybodaeth a chamwybodaeth sylweddol mewn perthynas â thai cymdeithasol a'r ddadl ehangach am fewnfudo yng Nghymru. Mae'n bwysig pwysleisio bod dyraniadau tai cymdeithasol yn gweithio'n bennaf i wasanaethu pobl Cymru. Y gwir amdani yw bod awdurdodau lleol ledled Cymru yn cymhwyso mesurau rheoli llym ynghylch cymhwystra, ac mae angen dilyn y broses gywir bob amser i sicrhau bod anghenion o ran tai'n cael eu hasesu'n briodol.

Mae cymdeithasau tai hefyd yn chwarae rôl gynyddol bwysig yn cefnogi pobl a chymunedau, gan helpu preswylwyr i gynnal eu tenantiaethau, gwella eu lles, a chael mynediad at gyfleoedd sy'n eu galluogi i ffynnu. O ganlyniad, mae landlordiaid cymdeithasol yn cydbwyso'r angen i adeiladu mwy o gartrefi, buddsoddi mewn cartrefi sy'n bodoli'n barod, a darparu gwasanaethau sy'n ymateb i heriau cymdeithasol ac economaidd ehangach. Geilw hyn am fuddsoddiad cryf, buddsoddiad hirdymor ac ymrwymiad ar y cyd i fynd i'r afael ag anghenion o ran tai yng Nghymru. Nid y meini prawf cymhwystra yw'r her fwyaf sy'n wynebu'r system dai yng Nghymru, ond yr angen i fuddsoddi mewn mwy o gartrefi cymdeithasol.

Yn nhymor y Senedd ddiwethaf, buddsoddodd Llywodraeth Lafur Cymru £2 biliwn i ddarparu mwy na 20,000 o gartrefi i'w gosod ar rent yn y sector cymdeithasol, a dyna'r lefelau buddsoddi uchaf erioed a'r lefelau cyflawni uchaf erioed. Hoffwn wybod sut y mae'r Llywodraeth bresennol yn mynd i gynnal y momentwm hwnnw a chynyddu'r cyflenwad o dai cymdeithasol ledled Cymru, gan leihau'r rhestr aros am dai cymdeithasol. Dylai Llywodraeth Cymru ganolbwyntio ar adeiladu mwy o gartrefi, dod ag eiddo gwag yn ôl i ddefnydd, a sicrhau bod cynghorau a chymdeithasau tai'n gallu datblygu cynlluniau i gynyddu'r cyflenwad o dai cymdeithasol. Ar hynny y dylai'r Senedd hon ganolbwyntio a'i graffu.

Yn olaf, Weinidog Cabinet, mae yna ymdrechion i godi bwganod yn y Siambr hon heddiw, felly beth y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn ei wneud i herio'r dwyllwybodaeth a'r gamwybodaeth ynghylch cymhwystra i gael tai cymdeithasol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Llywydd. Llywydd, the Member for Caerdydd Penarth has set out the principle. I will set out what it looks like on a street in Bangor. A house that used to hold a family now holds six men who arrived in this country as adults. The bins overflow, the parking goes, the neighbours stop letting their children play outside, and when the neighbours complain, they're told they are the problem. 

This is not a housing policy; it's a choice to socialise the cost of a failed system, a transfer of the cost from the people who made the decision to the people who live next door to it. HMOs for foreign nationals have become the mechanism by which hard political choices are avoided. Wales does not have a spare stock of family homes. We have long waiting lists. We have young couples forced to live with their parents into their 30s. We have veterans and key workers who can't get housing in the town where they were born. And we have a licensing regime for HMOs that's treating it as a growth industry.

Every family home converted into a HMO is a home taken out of the market for a local family and put into a market that pays better, where the tenants are transient, the houses are crowded, and rental income is backed by a public contract. Landlords did not invent this incentive—Government did. So, let us be precise about what this motion does and does not do.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Lywydd, mae'r Aelod dros Gaerdydd Penarth wedi nodi'r egwyddor. Fe wnaf i nodi sut mae'n edrych ar stryd ym Mangor. Mae tŷ a arferai gynnwys teulu bellach yn cynnwys chwech o ddynion a gyrhaeddodd y wlad hon fel oedolion. Mae'r biniau'n gorlifo, mae'r llefydd parcio'n mynd, mae'r cymdogion yn rhoi'r gorau i adael i'w plant chwarae tu allan, a phan fo'r cymdogion yn cwyno, dywedir wrthynt mai nhw yw'r broblem.

Nid polisi tai yw hwn, ond dewis i gymdeithasoli cost system fethedig, trosglwyddo'r gost oddi wrth y bobl a wnaeth y penderfyniad i'r bobl sy'n byw drws nesaf iddo. Mae tai amlfeddiannaeth ar gyfer gwladolion tramor wedi dod yn fecanwaith lle mae dewisiadau gwleidyddol anodd yn cael eu hosgoi. Nid oes gan Gymru stoc sbâr o gartrefi teuluol. Mae gennym restrau aros hir. Mae gennym gyplau ifanc sy'n cael eu gorfodi i fyw gyda'u rhieni yn eu 30au. Mae gennym gyn-filwyr a gweithwyr allweddol na allant gael tai yn y dref lle cawsant eu geni. Ac mae gennym gyfundrefn drwyddedu tai amlfeddiannaeth sy'n ei drin fel diwydiant twf.

Mae pob cartref teuluol a gafodd ei droi'n dŷ amlfeddiannaeth yn gartref sy'n cael ei dynnu allan o'r farchnad i deulu lleol a'i roi mewn marchnad sy'n talu'n well, lle mae'r tenantiaid yn rhai dros dro, y tai'n orlawn, a lle caiff incwm rhent ei gefnogi gan gontract cyhoeddus. Nid landlordiaid a ddyfeisiodd y cymhelliant hwn, ond Llywodraeth. Felly, gadewch inni fod yn fanwl gywir ynglŷn â'r hyn y mae'r cynnig hwn yn ei wneud ac nad yw'n ei wneud.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. So, would you agree that we shouldn't be placing that issue onto more vulnerable people, particularly people who are seeking asylum in the United Kingdom and end up in Wales? And so, we're just combating these two groups that are both in need of housing, when the issue itself is what needs to be resolved in supporting people who do actually deserve to have housing. We should have enough appropriate housing for everybody to live a safe life.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Felly, a fyddech chi'n cytuno na ddylem osod y broblem honno ar bobl fwy agored i niwed, yn enwedig pobl sy'n ceisio lloches yn y Deyrnas Unedig ac yn dod i ben eu taith yng Nghymru? XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
If we had unlimited money, I'd agree with you, but we don't have unlimited money and we have vulnerable people in this country. They should be prioritised.

In Gwynedd alone, we have over 2,000 local people in need of social housing, often waiting for over two years. This motion will simply ensure people who already belong to this country have priority. Reform has been clear. Foreign nationals should not be in social housing. The order of priority should be British families with children, British veterans, British workers. This motion simply asks the Government to stop pretending that eligibility is somebody else's problem, even as constituents are pushed aside.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
—from Manchester.

The order of priority should be British—. Well, actually, where Westminster—. Okay, this motion simply asks the Government to stop pretending that eligibility is somebody else's problem. Where Westminster holds the power to act, this Government must use its influence to ensure Westminster respects the interests of the Welsh people.

The Senedd could also make it harder to dodge the local connection test for housing. Gwynedd already uses one: five years residence, or a close family member resident for 10 years, or five years of work in the community. We could set a Wales-wide minimum qualification period, stop short placement counting as a connection, and require a local connection to outweigh other factors.

Some Members may try and claim that this is unfair. I will tell you what is unfair. It is unfair that a person who has paid tax into the system for decades can wait longer for housing than somebody who has just arrived. It is unfair that a street in Bangor absorbs the disorder while people who designed the nation of sanctuary live nowhere near it.

It is dishonest to pretend that every arrival is a net contributor. Some are; many in the HMO system are not. A housing policy that cannot tell the difference or simply ignores these outcomes is not compassion; it is an invoice sent to my constituents, paid not only with money but also by sacrificing community cohesion. In a world where Government is spending more than it can afford, where the reality of scarcity is a growing fact of life, the moral duty is first to our people and then to the people of the world.

This choice is now becoming acute and urgent. HMOs must not be used as a solution for our failure to control our borders. We have done more than enough. The test now is whether this Chamber will say so. I support this motion.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
—o Fanceinion.

Dylai trefn y flaenoriaeth olygu pobl Brydeinig—. Wel, mewn gwirionedd, lle mae San Steffan—. Iawn, mae'r cynnig hwn yn gofyn i'r Llywodraeth roi'r gorau i esgus bod cymhwystra'n broblem i rywun arall. Lle mae gan San Steffan bŵer i weithredu, rhaid i'r Llywodraeth hon ddefnyddio ei dylanwad i sicrhau bod San Steffan yn parchu buddiannau pobl Cymru.

Gallai'r Senedd hefyd ei gwneud hi'n anos osgoi'r prawf cysylltiad lleol ar gyfer tai. Mae Gwynedd eisoes yn defnyddio un: pum mlynedd o breswyliad, neu aelod agos o'r teulu sydd wedi preswylio ers 10 mlynedd, neu bum mlynedd o waith yn y gymuned. Gallwn osod isafswm cyfnod cymhwystra ledled Cymru, rhoi'r gorau i gyfrif lleoliad byr fel cysylltiad, a gwneud cysylltiad lleol yn ofynnol i orbwyso ffactorau eraill.

Efallai y bydd rhai Aelodau'n ceisio honni bod hyn yn annheg. Fe ddywedaf wrthych beth sy'n annheg. Mae'n annheg fod unigolyn sydd wedi talu treth i mewn i'r system ers degawdau yn gallu aros yn hirach am dŷ na rhywun sydd newydd gyrraedd. Mae'n annheg fod stryd ym Mangor yn amsugno'r anhrefn tra nad yw'r bobl a gynlluniodd y genedl noddfa'n byw unman yn agos at yr anhrefn hwnnw.

Mae'n anonest esgus bod pob unigolyn sy'n cyrraedd yn gyfrannwr net. Mae rhai; mae llawer yn y system dai amlfeddiannaeth nad ydynt yn gyfranwyr net. Nid tosturi yw polisi tai nad yw'n gallu gwahaniaethu rhwng, neu sy'n anwybyddu'r canlyniadau hyn; mae'n anfoneb a anfonir at fy etholwyr, a delir nid yn unig gydag arian ond hefyd trwy aberthu cydlyniant cymunedol. Mewn byd lle mae Llywodraeth yn gwario mwy nag y gall ei fforddio, lle mae realiti prinder yn ffaith bywyd gynyddol, mae'r ddyletswydd foesol yn gyntaf i'n pobl ni ac yna i bobl y byd.

Mae'r dewis hwn bellach yn dod yn acíwt ac yn fater o frys. Ni ddylid defnyddio tai amlfeddiannaeth fel ateb i'n methiant i reoli ein ffiniau. Rydym wedi gwneud mwy na digon. Y prawf nawr yw a fydd y Siambr hon yn dweud hynny. Rwy'n cefnogi'r cynnig hwn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I will try and be brief because I fear that just like this isn't the first time we've ended our day having this sort of debate, it won't be the last time that we have to stand up at the end of the day and rebut this ugly, divisive and hateful rhetoric. I am ashamed that we have to keep having this discussion. Going back to something that was said earlier today by the Minister: everyone has the right to a safe and adequate home. Everyone. Without it, how can you begin to build a life? How can you begin to participate and contribute to society? How can you begin to choose to call Wales your home as so many of us have? I repeat: the right to safe and adequate housing for everyone is a key test for this Senedd.

As I say, it's disappointing to see yet again more divisive rhetoric from the usual suspects in this Siambr, who are using—[Interruption.]—I can shout louder than you, believe me—what is a basic human right to stoke fear in our communities and cause division. Shame on you. When we say HMOs, the image that might come to mind may not be particularly pretty. But this image of what can be some of the worst quality, unsafe, overcrowded homes is now being used by Reform once again to scaremonger people about perceived dangers in their communities.

The situation in some HMOs isn't ideal. That doesn't take anything away from the fact that everyone deserves a place to live—a safe, secure and warm place to live. Due to the lack of social homes that so many of our colleagues have mentioned, people are stuck in the cheapest, inadequate private housing options. And Reform are disgracefully arguing again that we need to look after our own—what do the words even mean—while ignoring the fundamental problem that there are not enough good-quality, affordable homes for everyone who needs one. And I would like to pay credit again to the housing Minister for making that point so clearly earlier on today.

Foreign nationals or not, everyone needs somewhere to live. It is their human right. We need more social housing that meets the needs of everyone in our communities. Scarcity must not be used to pit communities against one another.

This motion is nonsensical, hateful and inflammatory. And words have real consequences. I have said this time and time again in this Siambr, but, sadly, it bears repeating. [Interruption.] No. Divisive rhetoric, such as we've heard today, only stands to cause division in our communities. And this fearmongering is the sort of thing that leads people to feel even more unsafe in their homes and communities than they already do. People across Wales see this for what it is. They see you for what you're saying.

I represent the most diverse constituency in Wales, and its diversity makes Cardiff what it is today. People from around the world have chosen to make Cardiff their home, and the people of Cardiff will not allow you to divide our communities. People, time and time again, have stood up to this divisive rhetoric and shown solidarity with their neighbours.

Reform are not interested in community cohesion. Reform are not interested in finding housing solutions. Reform are only interested in dividing our communities to distract from the fact that you have no answers to the problems facing the people of Wales. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe geisiaf fod yn fyr oherwydd, er nad dyma'r tro cyntaf inni orffen ein diwrnod gyda dadl o'r fath, rwy'n ofni nad dyma fydd y tro olaf inni godi ar ddiwedd y dydd a gwrthsefyll y rhethreg hyll, ymrannol ac atgas hon. Mae arnaf gywilydd fod yn rhaid inni barhau i gael y drafodaeth hon. I fynd yn ôl at rywbeth a ddywedwyd yn gynharach heddiw gan y Gweinidog: mae gan bawb hawl i gartref diogel a digonol. Pawb. Hebddo, sut y gallwch chi ddechrau adeiladu bywyd? Sut y gallwch chi ddechrau cyfranogi a chyfrannu at gymdeithas? Sut y gallwch chi ddechrau dewis galw Cymru yn gartref fel y mae cymaint ohonom wedi'i wneud? Rwy'n ailadrodd: mae'r hawl i dai diogel a digonol i bawb yn brawf allweddol i'r Senedd hon.

Fel y dywedais, mae'n siomedig gweld mwy o rethreg ymrannol unwaith eto gan yr un hen rai yn y Siambr hon, sy'n defnyddio—[Torri ar draws.]—gallaf weiddi'n uwch na chi, credwch fi—yr hyn sy'n hawl ddynol sylfaenol i godi bwganod yn ein cymunedau ac achosi ymraniad. Cywilydd arnoch chi. Pan fyddwn yn dweud tai amlfeddiannaeth, efallai nad yw'r ddelwedd a allai ddod i'r meddwl yn arbennig o brydferth. Ond mae'r darlun o'r hyn a all fod yn rhai o'r cartrefi gwaethaf eu hansawdd, cartrefi anniogel a gorlawn, bellach yn cael ei ddefnyddio gan Reform unwaith eto i godi bwganod am beryglon canfyddedig yn eu cymunedau.

Nid yw'r sefyllfa mewn rhai tai amlfeddiannaeth yn ddelfrydol. Nid yw hynny'n tynnu oddi wrth y ffaith bod pawb yn haeddu lle i fyw—lle saff, diogel a chynnes i fyw. Oherwydd y diffyg cartrefi cymdeithasol y mae cymaint o'n cyd-Aelodau wedi'i grybwyll, mae pobl yn gyfyngedig i'r opsiynau tai preifat rhataf ac annigonol. Ac yn gywilyddus, mae Reform yn dadlau eto fod angen inni edrych ar ôl ein pobl ein hunain—beth yw ystyr y geiriau hyd yn oed—gan anwybyddu'r broblem sylfaenol nad oes digon o gartrefi fforddiadwy o ansawdd da i bawb sydd angen un. A hoffwn dalu clod eto i'r Gweinidog tai am wneud y pwynt hwnnw mor glir yn gynharach heddiw.

Gwladolion tramor neu beidio, mae angen rhywle i fyw ar bawb. Dyna yw eu hawl ddynol. Mae angen mwy o dai cymdeithasol arnom sy'n diwallu anghenion pawb yn ein cymunedau. Ni ddylid defnyddio prinder i osod cymunedau yn erbyn ei gilydd.

Mae'r cynnig hwn yn nonsens, yn atgas ac yn ymfflamychol. Ac mae canlyniadau go iawn i eiriau. Rwyf wedi dweud hyn dro ar ôl tro yn y Siambr hon, ond yn anffodus, rhaid ei ailadrodd. [Torri ar draws.] Na. Nid yw rhethreg ymrannol, fel yr hyn a glywsom heddiw, ond yn achosi rhaniadau yn ein cymunedau. A chodi bwganod yn y ffordd hon yw'r math o beth sy'n arwain pobl i deimlo hyd yn oed yn fwy anniogel yn eu cartrefi a'u cymunedau. Mae pobl ledled Cymru yn gweld hyn am yr hyn ydyw. Maent yn eich gweld chi am yr hyn rydych chi'n ei ddweud.

Rwy'n cynrychioli'r etholaeth fwyaf amrywiol yng Nghymru, a'i hamrywiaeth sy'n gwneud Caerdydd yr hyn ydyw heddiw. Mae pobl o bob cwr o'r byd wedi dewis gwneud Caerdydd yn gartref iddynt, ac ni fydd pobl Caerdydd yn caniatáu i chi rannu ein cymunedau. Mae pobl, dro ar ôl tro, wedi gwrthsefyll y rhethreg ymrannol hon ac wedi dangos undod â'u cymdogion.

Nid oes gan Reform ddiddordeb mewn cydlyniant cymunedol. Nid oes gan Reform ddiddordeb mewn dod o hyd i atebion tai. Nid oes gan Reform ddiddordeb mewn dim heblaw rhannu ein cymunedau i dynnu sylw oddi wrth y ffaith nad oes gennych chi atebion i'r problemau sy'n wynebu pobl Cymru. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I want to focus on the HMO element of this debate. My family and I live next door to a HMO and have done for the past 15 years. One in five of the homes in our street is a HMO. HMOs are private houses, not subsidised, and it's odd that a political party that professes to be for the free market should seek to limit that housing market. But I'll come back to why this is such an odd debate.

In a past life, I was vice-chair of planning on Wrexham council, and the issues of HMOs have been a hot potato for more than a decade—not for the reasons stated by the people over there, but because an overconcentration of HMOs can impact a community in terms of overdevelopment, highway matters and waste disposal.

Houses in multiple occupation are a small but integral part of the housing mix. They provide accommodation for people who can't afford a house or a flat, and there are loads of reasons for that. Let's hope that no-one here loses their job or income. Let's hope that no-one here has a health issue. Let's hope that no-one here has a messy divorce, a breakdown in the family or, God forbid, is forced to flee domestic violence or coercive control. These are all issues that can lead people to look for a housing option that suits them temporarily.

I won't go into other issues, because Kiera Marshall and Peter Fox have very eloquently mentioned them, but I'll mention one: students living away from home are living in HMOs. Does the Member want to prevent all foreign students from having accommodation? Do you? Perhaps you can talk to the vice-chancellors about what that would do to our Welsh universities.

As it happens, the owner of the HMO next to me is a responsible landlord, but there are unscrupulous landlords who are cramming in as many people as possible to maximise profits. That's the real issue with HMOs. In the wrong hands and without sufficient oversight, they become dumping grounds for people with very real problems of substance misuse and mental health issues, but without any support. You don't care about that, obviously. You're just concerned about the people who look and sound different to you.

People in my town are paying £87.50 a week for a shared room. There are eight other people in the house, with no communal space, apart from a family kitchen and a small back garden. That's not the fault of tenants, it's the fault of those unscrupulous landlords who fail to treat tenants as human beings. And these are working people, not on benefits. They're nurses, they're care workers, they're people I hear getting up at 6 o'clock in the morning to go to the industrial estate.

I said earlier that this focus on a certain type of housing was odd. I think we know why—people have told us why very eloquently. The track record of the party involved is all about seeking to divide and rule, fuelled by hatred, not compassion. Since the UK Government moved from housing asylum seekers and refugees in hotels—I believe there's one hotel in the whole of Wales now—those who were busy rioting, burning and hating outside those hotels have looked for a new focus, and they've found it, haven't they, in HMOs.

Like those unscrupulous landlords, they don't see the people who live in HMOs as human beings; they see them as inferior, as problems. What we've seen today is people deliberately conflating foreign nationals with asylum seekers, deliberately conflating people on benefits with foreign nationals. It's a mess of a debate. It's scaremongering and demonising for clickbait and social media. It's not a serious proposition; it virtue signals their hatred for people who look different, who sound different. It could be written in crayon.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ganolbwyntio ar elfen tai amlfeddiannaeth y ddadl hon. Mae fy nheulu a minnau wedi byw drws nesaf i dŷ amlfeddiannaeth ers 15 mlynedd. Mae un o bob pump cartref yn ein stryd yn dŷ amlfeddiannaeth. Tai preifat yw tai amlfeddiannaeth, nid tai cymorthdaledig, ac mae'n rhyfedd fod plaid wleidyddol sy'n honni ei bod o blaid y farchnad rydd yn ceisio cyfyngu ar y farchnad dai honno. Ond dof yn ôl at pam fod hon yn ddadl mor rhyfedd.

Mewn bywyd blaenorol, roeddwn yn is-gadeirydd cynllunio ar gyngor Wrecsam, ac mae materion tai amlfeddiannaeth wedi bod yn destun trafod ers dros ddegawd—nid am y rhesymau a nodwyd gan y bobl draw acw, ond oherwydd bod gorgrynhoad o dai amlfeddiannaeth yn gallu effeithio ar gymuned o ran gorddatblygu, materion priffyrdd a gwaredu gwastraff.

Mae tai amlfeddiannaeth yn rhan fach ond annatod o'r cymysgedd tai. Maent yn darparu llety i bobl na allant fforddio tŷ na fflat, ac mae llu o resymau dros hynny. Gadewch inni obeithio nad oes unrhyw un yma'n colli eu swydd na'u hincwm. Gadewch inni obeithio nad oes gan unrhyw un yma broblem iechyd. Gadewch inni obeithio nad oes unrhyw un yma'n cael ysgariad blêr, chwalfa deuluol, neu Duw a'n gwaredo, yn cael eu gorfodi i ffoi rhag trais domestig neu reolaeth drwy orfodaeth. Mae'r rhain oll yn faterion a all arwain pobl i chwilio am opsiwn tai sy'n addas ar eu cyfer dros dro.

Nid wyf am drafod materion eraill, am fod Kiera Marshall a Peter Fox wedi sôn amdanynt yn huawdl iawn, ond fe soniaf am un: mae myfyrwyr sy'n byw oddi cartref yn byw mewn tai amlfeddiannaeth. A yw'r Aelod eisiau atal pob myfyriwr tramor rhag cael llety? Ydych chi? Efallai y gallwch siarad â'r is-gangellorion ynglŷn â’r hyn y byddai hynny'n ei wneud i'n prifysgolion yng Nghymru.

Fel y mae'n digwydd, mae perchennog y tŷ amlfeddiannaeth drws nesaf i mi yn landlord cyfrifol, ond mae rhai landlordiaid diegwyddor yn gwasgu cymaint o bobl â phosibl i mewn i dŷ er mwyn gwneud mwy o elw. Dyna'r broblem go iawn gyda thai amlfeddiannaeth. Yn y dwylo anghywir a heb ddigon o oruchwyliaeth, maent yn dod yn feysydd dympio i bobl â phroblemau real iawn fel camddefnyddio sylweddau a phroblemau iechyd meddwl, ond heb unrhyw gefnogaeth. Mae'n amlwg nad ydych yn poeni am hynny. Rydych chi'n poeni am y bobl sy'n edrych ac yn swnio'n wahanol i chi.

Mae pobl yn fy nhref i'n talu £87.50 yr wythnos am ystafell a rennir. Mae wyth o bobl eraill yn y tŷ, heb unrhyw le cymunedol, ar wahân i gegin deuluol a gardd gefn fach. Nid bai'r tenantiaid yw hynny, ond bai landlordiaid diegwyddor nad ydynt yn trin tenantiaid fel bodau dynol. Ac mae'r rhain yn bobl sy'n gweithio, nid ar fudd-daliadau. Maent yn nyrsys, maent yn weithwyr gofal, maent yn bobl rwy'n eu clywed yn codi am 6 o'r gloch y bore i fynd i'r ystad ddiwydiannol.

Dywedais yn gynharach fod y ffocws hwn ar fath penodol o dai yn rhyfedd. Rwy'n credu ein bod yn gwybod pam—mae pobl wedi dweud wrthym yn huawdl iawn pam. Ceisio rhannu a rheoli yw hanes y blaid dan sylw, wedi'u tanio gan gasineb, nid tosturi. Ers i Lywodraeth y DU newid o gartrefu ceiswyr lloches a ffoaduriaid mewn gwestai—rwy'n credu mai un gwesty sydd yna yng Nghymru gyfan nawr—mae'r rhai a fu'n brysur yn codi twrw, yn llosgi ac yn casáu y tu allan i'r gwestai hynny wedi chwilio am ffocws newydd, ac maent wedi dod o hyd iddo, onid ydynt, ar ffurf tai amlfeddiannaeth.

Fel y landlordiaid diegwyddor hynny, nid ydynt yn gweld y bobl sy'n byw mewn tai amlfeddiannaeth fel bodau dynol; maent yn eu gweld fel pobl israddol, fel problemau. Yr hyn a welsom heddiw yw pobl yn fwriadol yn trafod gwladolion tramor a cheiswyr lloches fel pe baent yr un peth, yn fwriadol yn trafod pobl ar fudd-daliadau a gwladolion tramor fel pe baent yr un peth. Mae'n llanast o ddadl. Maent yn codi bwganod ac yn demoneiddio yn enw abwyd clicio a'r cyfryngau cymdeithasol. Nid yw'n gynnig difrifol; mae'n arwyddo'u casineb at bobl sy'n edrych yn wahanol, sy'n swnio'n wahanol. Gallai fod wedi'i ysgrifennu mewn creon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Before I begin, can I just say that the huge numbers of people who put these Members in these seats to represent their views need to have those views heard? Because you don't like them doesn't mean to say that those views are irrelevant. There have been enough interventions this afternoon to try and stop those views from being heard, so politely and respectfully, I won't be taking any during my speech.

Many of my constituents ask a simple question, Llywydd: who is housing for in Wales? They work, pay their taxes and raise their families here, yet when they need a secure, affordable home, too often the answer is to keep waiting. Shelter Cymru's 2025 research estimated that around 170,000 people, including approximately 45,000 children, are represented on social housing waiting lists. At the building rate used in that report, providing enough additional homes to meet that demand would take more than 35 years. That is a generation of unmet need. Children grow up, families struggle, people put their lives on hold, while the Government produces another promise.

Shelter Cymru attributes this crisis to decades of failing to build enough social homes. On that, they are right. But acknowledging that failure does not remove the need to make choices today. Building more homes and deciding who has access to them are both responsibilities of this Government. We must build more, faster, but construction takes time and our constituents need help now. Where homes are scarce, eligibility matters, priorities matter and British taxpayers are entitled to ask whether the system that they support puts their needs first. My answer is that it should. That includes British citizens who cannot work through disability, those caring for relatives, pensioners, children and, of course, our veterans. Putting our citizens first must mean protecting those who need support, as well as recognising those whose taxes sustain it. 

In Ceredigion Penfro, constituents tell me that they have worked here and paid in all of their working lives and raised families here, and still, they are told to wait. They deserve more than sympathy; they deserve a clear priority in housing policy. That goes beyond asylum accommodation, and we should say so plainly. The argument is about housing capacity and national priorities, not claiming that somebody's nationality determines their character.

Social housing is scarce. Reform UK believe that access should be reserved for British citizens. On HMOs, our stance is clear: immigration policy must reflect housing capacity and British citizens must come first. The Welsh and UK Governments must work together to deliver that policy with clear rules, a managed transition and firm enforcement.

Constituents have also raised concerns about what they describe—and these are my constituents' concerns—as asylum seekers arriving in HMOs after dark, with little explanation to neighbours. Arriving after dark does not establish wrongdoing, but silence from those responsible leaves fears growing and questions unanswered. Residents deserve information about management, occupancy, safeguards and who will respond when concerns arise. Those responsibilities apply whatever eligibility rules are adopted. Restricting access cannot replace proper enforcement. British taxpayers should not be an afterthought in the housing system that they sustain. That is why I support this motion. Build more homes, put British citizens first and make the Government answer for the decisions that it takes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Cyn imi ddechrau, a gaf i ddweud bod angen i'r niferoedd enfawr o bobl a roddodd yr Aelodau hyn yn y seddau hyn i gynrychioli eu safbwyntiau gael y safbwyntiau hynny wedi eu clywed? Nid yw'r ffaith nad ydych chi'n eu hoffi yn golygu bod y safbwyntiau hynny'n amherthnasol. Cafwyd digon o ymyriadau y prynhawn yma i geisio atal y safbwyntiau hynny rhag cael eu clywed, felly yn gwrtais ac yn barchus, ni fyddaf yn derbyn unrhyw ymyriadau eraill yn ystod fy araith.

Mae llawer o fy etholwyr yn gofyn cwestiwn syml, Lywydd: ar gyfer pwy y mae tai yng Nghymru? Maent yn gweithio, yn talu eu trethi ac yn magu eu teuluoedd yma, ond pan fydd angen cartref diogel a fforddiadwy arnynt, yr ateb yn rhy aml yw dal ati i aros. Amcangyfrifodd ymchwil Shelter Cymru yn 2025 fod oddeutu 170,000 o bobl, gan gynnwys oddeutu 45,000 o blant, ar restrau aros am dai cymdeithasol. Ar y gyfradd adeiladu a ddefnyddiwyd yn yr adroddiad hwnnw, byddai darparu digon o gartrefi ychwanegol i ateb y galw hwnnw'n cymryd mwy na 35 mlynedd. Dyna genhedlaeth o angen heb ei ddiwallu. Mae plant yn tyfu i fyny, mae teuluoedd yn ei chael hi'n anodd, mae pobl yn rhoi eu bywydau ar stop, tra bo'r Llywodraeth yn cynhyrchu addewid arall.

Mae Shelter Cymru yn rhoi'r bai am yr argyfwng hwn ar ddegawdau o fethu adeiladu digon o dai cymdeithasol. Ar hynny, maent yn gywir. Ond nid yw cydnabod y methiant hwnnw'n dileu'r angen i wneud dewisiadau heddiw. Mae adeiladu mwy o gartrefi a phenderfynu pwy sydd â mynediad atynt yn gyfrifoldebau i'r Llywodraeth hon. Mae’n rhaid inni adeiladu mwy, yn gyflymach, ond mae adeiladu'n cymryd amser ac mae angen cymorth ar ein hetholwyr nawr. Lle mae cartrefi'n brin, mae cymhwystra'n bwysig, mae blaenoriaethau'n bwysig ac mae gan drethdalwyr Prydain hawl i ofyn a yw'r system y maent yn ei chefnogi yn rhoi eu hanghenion nhw yn gyntaf. Fy ateb i yw y dylai. Mae hynny'n cynnwys dinasyddion Prydeinig na allant weithio oherwydd anabledd, y rhai sy'n gofalu am berthnasau, pensiynwyr, plant, ac wrth gwrs, ein cyn-filwyr. Mae'n rhaid i roi ein dinasyddion yn gyntaf olygu diogelu'r rhai sydd angen cymorth, yn ogystal â chydnabod y rhai y mae eu trethi yn cynnal y cymorth hwnnw.

Yng Ngheredigion Penfro, dywed etholwyr wrthyf eu bod wedi gweithio yma ac wedi bod yn talu drwy gydol eu hoes waith ac wedi magu teuluoedd yma, ac eto, dywedir wrthynt am ddal ati i aros. Maent yn haeddu mwy na chydymdeimlad; maent yn haeddu blaenoriaeth glir mewn polisi tai. Mae hynny'n mynd y tu hwnt i lety lloches, a dylem ddweud hynny'n blwmp ac yn blaen. Mae a wnelo'r ddadl â chapasiti tai a blaenoriaethau cenedlaethol, nid honni bod cenedligrwydd rhywun yn diffinio eu cymeriad.

Mae tai cymdeithasol yn brin. Mae Reform UK yn credu y dylid cadw mynediad ar gyfer dinasyddion Prydeinig. Ar dai amlfeddiannaeth, mae ein safbwynt yn glir: rhaid i bolisi mewnfudo adlewyrchu capasiti tai a rhaid rhoi dinasyddion Prydeinig yn gyntaf. Rhaid i Lywodraeth Cymru a Llywodraeth y DU gydweithio i gyflawni'r polisi hwnnw gyda rheolau clir, cyfnod pontio wedi'i reoli a gorfodaeth gadarn.

Mae etholwyr hefyd wedi codi pryderon ynghylch yr hyn y maent yn ei ddisgrifio—a dyma bryderon fy etholwyr—fel ceiswyr lloches yn cyrraedd tai amlfeddiannaeth ar ôl iddi nosi, heb fawr o esboniad i gymdogion. Nid yw cyrraedd ar ôl iddi nosi yn gamwedd, ond mae distawrwydd gan y rhai sy'n gyfrifol yn peri i ofnau dyfu ac yn gadael cwestiynau heb eu hateb. Mae preswylwyr yn haeddu gwybodaeth am reolaeth, meddiannaeth, mesurau diogelwch a phwy fydd yn ymateb pan fydd pryderon yn codi. Mae'r cyfrifoldebau hynny'n berthnasol pa bynnag reolau cymhwystra a gaiff eu mabwysiadu. Ni all cyfyngu mynediad gymryd lle gorfodaeth briodol. Ni ddylai trethdalwyr Prydeinig fod yn ôl-ystyriaeth yn y system dai y maent yn ei chynnal. Dyna pam fy mod yn cefnogi'r cynnig hwn. Adeiladwch fwy o gartrefi, rhowch ddinasyddion Prydeinig yn gyntaf a gwnewch y Llywodraeth yn atebol am y penderfyniadau y mae'n eu gwneud.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Unfortunately, I will not be able to call all Members in this debate within the time allocated for it. Before I call on the Cabinet Minister to respond, I understand that we may have a point of order.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llywydd, I'd like to raise a point of order about the proposing Member's speech at the beginning. I believe that there was an error of fact and I invite the Member, in her response, to correct that. There was a conflation of nation, nationality and citizenship. The census provides us with accurate data on social rented housing in Cardiff and can be accessed by all Members on the census website. Of social rented housing, there were 19,400 UK passport holders, and 1,800—less than 10 per cent—who held other passports. Of rented from the local authority, there were 19,605 UK passport holders. Other passport holders were 1,848. So, I invite the Member, as a matter of order, to correct the record. Passport holders are those numbers. I believe the Member was talking about self-described nationality. Diolch, Lywydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Lywydd, hoffwn godi pwynt o drefn ynglŷn ag araith yr Aelod a wnaeth y cynnig ar y dechrau. Credaf fod yno gamgymeriad ffeithiol ac rwy'n gwahodd yr Aelod, yn ei hymateb, i gywiro hynny. Roedd yn trafod cenedl, cenedligrwydd a dinasyddiaeth fel pe baent yr un peth. Mae'r cyfrifiad yn rhoi data cywir i ni ar dai rhent cymdeithasol yng Nghaerdydd, a gall pob Aelod ddod o hyd iddo ar wefan y cyfrifiad. O ran tai rhent cymdeithasol, roedd 19,400 o ddeiliaid pasbort y DU, a 1,800—llai na 10 y cant—yn ddeiliad pasbortau eraill. O ran tai rhent yr awdurdod lleol, roedd 19,605 yn ddeiliaid pasbort y DU. Roedd 1,848 yn ddeiliaid pasbortau eraill. Felly, rwy'n gwahodd yr Aelod, fel mater o drefn, i gywiro'r cofnod. Deiliaid pasbort yw'r niferoedd hynny. Rwy'n credu bod yr Aelod yn sôn am genedligrwydd hunanddiffiniedig. Diolch, Lywydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr, Lywydd. Dwi'n gwrthod y cynnig yma yn gryf. Diolch i Lynne Neagle am gydgyflwyno'r gwelliant. Dwi'n falch o gydweithio ar fater mor bwysig. Mae nod y Llywodraeth yma yn glir. Dylai pawb yng Nghymru gael mynediad at gartref diogel, cynnes a fforddiadwy. Fe all tai amlfeddianaeth, HMOs, o ansawdd da chwarae rhan yn hynny, cyn belled â'u bod yn cael eu rheoleiddio a'u rheoli'n lleol. Rhaid i benderfyniadau am dai cymdeithasol ddilyn ein fframwaith cyfreithiol, a rhaid iddyn nhw fod yn deg ac yn adlewyrchu'r angen am dai—hynny ydy, anghenion pawb sy'n gymwys yn gyfreithiol i fyw yma yng Nghymru.

Dwi yn deall y rhwystredigaeth sy'n cael ei hachosi drwy aros yn hir am dai a gan gartrefi sy'n cael eu rheoli'n wael. Yr ateb ydy cynyddu'r cyflenwad o dai cyhoeddus, atal digartrefedd, cynnal safonau a chefnogi awdurdodau lleol, nid rhannu cymunedau na gosod grwpiau o bobl yn erbyn ei gilydd. Mae'r ciw am gartrefi cymdeithasol yn rhy hir, ond peidiwch â chreu rhaniadau diangen. Peidiwch â gosod pobl mewn angen yn erbyn ei gilydd. Yn hytrach, gweithiwn efo'n gilydd i greu mwy o gartrefi cyhoeddus i Gymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much, Llywydd. I strongly reject this motion. Thank you to Lynne Neagle for co-tabling the amendment. I was pleased to work with her on such an important issue. The Government's aim is clear. Everyone in Wales should have access to a safe, warm and affordable home. HMOs of good quality can play a part in that, as long as they are regulated and managed locally. Decisions on social housing must follow our legal framework, and they must be fair and reflect housing need—that is, the needs of everyone who legally qualifies to live here in Wales.

I do understand the frustration that can be caused by long waits for housing and by poorly managed homes. The solution is to increase the supply of social housing, prevent homelessness, uphold standards and support local authorities, not to divide communities or to pit groups of people against each other. The queue for social housing is too long, but don't create unnecessary division. Don't pit people in need against each other. Rather, we should work together to create more social homes in Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Reform says, 'End access to social housing for foreign nationals.' That's your policy. Does that mean that families who have a legal right to be here—families and their children—would be asked to leave their homes, turfed out onto the streets? Well, yes, I got the answer from Joe Martin. He said exactly that. They'd have three months. They would have three months to leave. That is what you said. That is an inhumane proposition, and it's a very, very sad day for this Senedd to hear those comments.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Reform yn dweud y byddent yn 'rhoi diwedd ar fynediad at dai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor.' Dyna eich polisi. A yw hynny'n golygu y byddai gofyn i deuluoedd sydd â hawl gyfreithiol i fod yma—teuluoedd a'u plant—adael eu cartrefi, a chael eu taflu allan ar y strydoedd? Wel, wrth gwrs, fe gefais yr ateb gan Joe Martin. Dywedodd yn union hynny. Byddai ganddynt dri mis. Byddai ganddynt dri mis i adael. Dyna a ddywedoch chi. Mae hwnnw'n gynnig annynol, ac mae'n ddiwrnod trist iawn i'r Senedd hon glywed y sylwadau hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae'r cynnig gan Reform yn galw am gyfyngu ar fynediad at dai cymdeithasol ar sail cenedligrwydd. Allwn ni ddim, wrth gwrs, gefnogi'r cynnig yma. Mae tai cymdeithasol yn cael eu dyrannu ar sail yr angen am dai ymhlith y rhai sy'n gymwys yn gyfreithiol. Dydyn nhw ddim yn cael eu dyrannu ar sail cenedligrwydd, ethnigrwydd na man geni. Mae deddfwriaeth eisoes yn rheoli'r hawl i gael tai cymdeithasol. Mae statws mewnfudo a man preswylio cyfreithlon eisoes yn ystyriaethau allweddol sy'n cael eu defnyddio i benderfynu ar gymhwystra rhywun. Dim ond pobl sydd â'r hawl i aros sydd yn gymwys i gael cymorth tai a thai cymdeithasol.

Dydy tai cymdeithasol ddim yn cael eu dyrannu i bobl sy'n ceisio lloches. Rydyn ni wedi clywed hynna dro ar ôl tro. Mae Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig yn darparu llety dros dro tra bo cais yn cael ei ystyried. Os bydd rhywun yn cael statws ffoadur—a dwi'n atgoffa'r Aelodau fod hynny'n golygu bod Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig wedi canfod bod yr unigolyn wedi ffoi rhag rhyfel, ofn neu erledigaeth—yna gallan nhw wneud cais am gymorth tai o dan yr un rheolau ag aelwydydd eraill.

Mae'r cynnig yma, felly, yn camliwio'r system bresennol. Mae'r her sy'n ein hwynebu ni yn ymwneud â chyflenwad tai, a'r ateb ydy adeiladu mwy o gartrefi a gwneud y defnydd gorau o'r cartrefi sydd ar gael. Lle mae polisi Reform ar gynyddu'r cyflenwad o dai cymdeithasol? Does gennych chi ddim polisi ynglŷn â hynny. Dydy pobl sydd yn chwilio am noddfa a phobl o wledydd eraill sy'n byw yn gyfreithlon yng Nghymru ddim yn cael unrhyw ffafriaeth o ran tai, a dydyn nhw ddim yn gyfrifol am y prinder tai fforddiadwy rydyn ni'n ei brofi ar hyn o bryd. Ac mae achosion y pwysau ar y cyflenwad tai yng Nghymru'n gymhleth, wedi bodoli ers amser maith, a dydy o ddim yn gwneud synnwyr—dydy'r ffeithiau ddim yn cyd-fynd â'r awgrym bod modd datrys yr heriau drwy eithrio grwpiau penodol. Dydy gwneud i grwpiau gwahanol gystadlu â'i gilydd ddim yn creu cartrefi nac yn lleihau pwysau ar wasanaethau.

Mi wnaf i droi wrth gloi at dai amlfeddiannaeth. Math o gartrefi sy'n cael eu rhannu ydy'r rhain, nid categori mewnfudo. Maen nhw'n darparu cartref i fyfyrwyr, gweithwyr proffesiynol ifanc a phobl eraill sydd angen tai, a dim ond lleiafrif bach sy'n cael eu defnyddio i letya ceiswyr lloches. Mae gan Gymru system reoleiddio glir. Mae angen trwydded ar gartrefi sy'n cael eu rhannu sydd o faint mwy ac yn wynebu risg uwch, ac fe all awdurdodau lleol ehangu'r gofynion trwyddedu pan fydd y dystiolaeth leol yn cyfiawnhau hynny. Fe allan nhw osod amodau, archwilio eiddo, gofyn am welliannau, gosod cosbau, atal cartrefi anniogel rhag cael eu defnyddio, ac erlyn landlordiaid. Fe allan nhw hefyd ddefnyddio pwerau cynllunio pan fydd hynny'n briodol.

Dydy llety sy'n cael ei ddefnyddio ar gyfer pobl sy'n ceisio lloches ddim wedi'i eithrio rhag gofynion cynllunio neu drwyddedu, ond yr awdurdodau lleol sydd yn y sefyllfa orau i ddefnyddio'r pwerau hyn am eu bod nhw'n deall y sefyllfa dai lleol a'r pwysau ar gymunedau. Dŷn ni yn parhau i weithio efo cynghorau a Chymdeithas Llywodraeth Leol Cymru i asesu a ydy'r fframwaith yn effeithiol ac a oes angen cymorth pellach, a dwi wedi gwneud yn glir y dylai trwyddedu amddiffyn preswylwyr a sicrhau camau rheoli priodol.

Mae'n safbwynt ni'n hollol glir: mae tai cymdeithasol yn cael eu dyrannu yn ôl yr angen ac yn unol â phwy sy'n gymwys yn ôl y gyfraith. Mae awdurdodau lleol yn rheoli prosesau trwyddedu a chynllunio mewn perthynas â thai amlfeddiannaeth o fewn y fframwaith cenedlaethol. Y Swyddfa Gartref sy'n penderfynu ble mae llety i geiswyr lloches yn cael ei ddarparu. Mae'r cynnig gwreiddiol yn awgrymu dull o ymdrin â phroblem dai gymhleth sydd yn llawer iawn rhy syml ac yn creu rhwygiadau. Mae gwelliant y Llywodraeth, efo cefnogaeth Lynne Neagle a'r grŵp Llafur, yn adlewyrchu'r gyfraith, yn parchu cyfrifoldebau pob haen o lywodraeth ac yn canolbwyntio ar gamau gweithredu a all wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol. Felly, dwi'n gofyn i'r Aelodau wrthod y cynnig a chefnogi gwelliant y Llywodraeth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
The Reform motion calls for a restriction on access to social housing on the grounds of nationality. We cannot, of course, support that proposal. Social housing is allocated on the basis of housing need among those who are legally eligible. It's not allocated on the basis of nationality, ethnicity, or place of birth. Legislation already controls the right to social housing. Immigration status and legal residence are already key considerations by which to determine someone's eligibility. It's only people who have the right to remain who are eligible for housing support and social housing.

Social housing is not allocated to people seeking asylum. We've heard that time and again. The UK Government provides temporary accommodation while a claim is considered. If someone is granted refugee status—and I remind Members that this means that the UK Government has found that the individual has fled from war, fear or persecution—then they may seek housing assistance under the same rules as other households.

This motion, therefore, misrepresents the current system. The challenge we face is one of housing supply, and the solution is to build more homes and make the best possible use of the homes that we have. Where is the Reform policy on increasing the supply of social homes? You have no policy on that. People seeking sanctuary and people from other countries who live lawfully in Wales do not get any preferential treatment for housing, and they are not responsible for the shortage of affordable housing that we are currently experiencing. And the causes of the pressure on housing stock in Wales are complex and have existed for a long time, and it makes no sense—the facts don't actually back up that we can actually solve the problem by exempting a particular group. Making different groups compete with each other doesn't create housing or reduce pressure on services.

I will turn in conclusion to HMOs. These are shared homes, not an immigration category. They provide homes for students, young professionals and others who need housing, and only a small minority are used to house asylum seekers. Wales has a clear regulation system. You need a licence for HMOs, which are larger and face greater risks, and local authorities can expand the licensing requirement when local factors justify that. They can place conditions, search properties, they can penalise and prevent unsafe accommodation from being used, and they can prosecute landlords. They can also use planning powers when appropriate.

Accommodation used for asylum seekers is not exempted from planning or licensing requirements, but it's local authorities who are best placed to use those powers because they understand the local housing situation and the pressure on communities. We continue to work with councils and the Welsh Local Government Association to assess whether the framework is effective and whether further support is required, and I have made it clear that licensing should protect residents and ensure appropriate regulation.

Our stance is quite clear: social housing is allocated according to need, in accordance with who qualifies through law. Local authorities manage licensing and planning processes in relation to HMOs within the national framework. The Home Office decides where asylum accommodation is provided. The original motion suggests a simplistic and divisive approach to a complex housing problem. The Government's amendment, with the support of Lynne Neagle and the Labour group, reflects the law, respects the responsibility of each level of government and focuses on actions that can make a real difference. I therefore ask Members to reject the motion and support the Government's amendment.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 8. Dadl Reform UK: Mynediad at dai amlfeddiannaeth a thai cymdeithasol i wladolion tramor
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. May I begin by thanking all Members across the Chamber who have contributed to a lively debate? Let me focus immediately on the people at the heart of this debate: those whose interests Reform believe are in urgent need of our support, the Welsh people.

At the end of the summer, 1,954 homeless people, including 102 children, were living in temporary hostel accommodation. A further 2,539 people, including 268 children, were in hotels and bed and breakfasts. That is nearly 4,500 people in Wales without a proper home of their own, nearly 400 children without the security that a proper home provides, and in too many cases without a bedroom of their own.

Those are not abstract figures, they are the families whose lives are put on hold because our social housing system is failing to meet their need. Housing is a finite resource—there are only so many homes available at any one time. In the midst of a housing crisis, it is the duty of this Senedd, of the Welsh Government, to decide fairly who should get priority. The position of Reform is plain: Welsh homes should go to Welsh people first, and social housing should serve people with the longest established link to Wales and the United Kingdom. But let me also be clear about what this means: EU nationals who have been granted settled status here have a lawful right to reside here. Reform respects that, and they would not be the target of this policy. Our concern is with a system that can put recent overseas arrivals ahead of the British and Welsh families who have lived, worked, paid taxes and raised their children here, only to find themselves in temporary accommodation or unable to secure a home in their own town. We must not allow subsidised social housing to become a further incentive for people to come here illegally from abroad. At a time when Welsh families are living in hostels, hotels and B&Bs, the first duty of Government must be to the people it is elected to serve.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. A gaf i ddechrau drwy ddiolch i bob Aelod ar draws y Siambr sydd wedi cyfrannu at ddadl fywiog? Gadewch imi ganolbwyntio ar unwaith ar y bobl sydd wrth wraidd y ddadl hon: y bobl y mae Reform o'r farn fod eu buddiannau angen ein cefnogaeth ar frys, sef pobl Cymru.

Ar ddiwedd yr haf, roedd 1,954 o bobl ddigartref, gan gynnwys 102 o blant, yn byw mewn llety hostel dros dro. Roedd 2,539 o bobl eraill, gan gynnwys 268 o blant, mewn gwestai a llety gwely a brecwast. Mae hynny'n golygu bron i 4,500 o bobl yng Nghymru heb gartref priodol eu hunain, bron i 400 o blant heb y diogelwch y mae cartref priodol yn ei ddarparu, ac mewn gormod o achosion, heb ystafell wely eu hunain.

Nid ffigurau haniaethol yw'r rhain, dyma'r teuluoedd y mae eu bywydau ar stop am nad yw ein system dai cymdeithasol yn diwallu eu hanghenion. Mae tai'n adnodd cyfyngedig—dim ond hyn a hyn o gartrefi sydd ar gael ar unrhyw adeg. Yng nghanol argyfwng tai, dyletswydd y Senedd hon, Llywodraeth Cymru, yw penderfynu'n deg pwy ddylai gael blaenoriaeth. Mae safbwynt Reform yn glir: dylai cartrefi Cymru fynd i bobl Cymru yn gyntaf, a dylai tai cymdeithasol wasanaethu pobl sydd â'r cysylltiad sefydledig hwyaf â Chymru a'r Deyrnas Unedig. Ond gadewch imi ddweud yn glir hefyd beth y mae hyn yn ei olygu: mae gan ddinasyddion yr UE sydd wedi cael statws preswylwyr sefydlog yma hawl gyfreithiol i breswylio yma. Mae Reform yn parchu hynny, ac nid nhw fyddai'n cael eu targedu gan y polisi hwn. Yr hyn sy'n peri pryder i ni yw system sy'n gallu blaenoriaethu dyfodiaid tramor diweddar ar draul y teuluoedd Prydeinig a Chymreig sydd wedi byw, gweithio, talu trethi a magu eu plant yma, ac sy'n gorfod byw mewn llety dros dro neu'n methu sicrhau cartref yn eu tref eu hunain. Rhaid inni beidio â chaniatáu i dai cymdeithasol cymorthdaledig ddod yn gymhelliant pellach i bobl ddod yma o dramor yn anghyfreithlon. Ar adeg pan fo teuluoedd Cymru'n byw mewn hosteli, gwestai a llety gwely a brecwast, rhaid i ddyletswydd gyntaf Llywodraeth fod i'r bobl y cafodd ei hethol i'w gwasanaethu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 8. Reform UK Debate: Access to HMOs and social housing for foreign nationals
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We have heard important contributions from colleagues. Joe Martin offered a prospect that I'm sure many on other sides of the Chamber would be pleased to see: him moving to China. [Laughter.] However, should he move there, he would have to find his own house. He would not be housed at the cost of the Chinese state. Our moral responsibility is to put the Welsh and British people first. John Clark rightly highlighted that it is unfair that a person who has paid taxes to our country for decades can be waiting longer for a house than those who have just arrived. And Francesca O'Brien shared some serious—[Interruption.] I think we've had quite enough interventions today, thank you. She shared some serious figures highlighting the scale of this issue and a lack of transparency from some local authorities.

I'd like to take a moment to respond to some of the other comments that have been made, starting off with the leader of Welsh Labour. For clarity, Suella Braverman was born in London and is a British citizen, so would be entitled to social housing under this policy. Peter—[Interruption.] Peter, as I've just clarified, EU citizens are not impacted by this policy when they have settled status, although I must say it is hard to take lessons from the Tories about seriousness on immigration. Kiera, the right to buy—[Interruption.] The right to buy gives people the chance to own their own home, one of the greatest equalisers of wealth this country has ever seen. Now, can it be done differently? Of course it can be done differently. But selling one social house can give you the equity to build three more. To simply say that we will not allow—[Interruption.] To simply say that we will not allow working families the opportunity to get on the housing ladder and own their own home is nonsensical. Jayne, it is not divisive to say that the Welsh Government should put the Welsh people first. And to the leader of the Welsh Greens, there is nothing more ugly and hateful than your party declaring that believing that the state of Israel can exist is racist.

Of course, reforming allocations alone is not the whole answer. We need to build more homes, but here, too, Wales is being failed. Minister, you spoke about the importance of house building. However, we have exchanged very recently frustrations with the planning system. Planning decisions take months and sometimes years, holding up investment and house building. Rather than acting now to relieve the pressure on planning departments, the Welsh Government has embarked on a three-year review of the national planning framework. Wales cannot afford another three years adrift. The backlog is already severe. The Bevan Foundation estimates that Wales is short of some 9,600 homes. That is the equivalent of building another Llandudno, another Bangor, nearly building a whole other Rhyl. These homes were needed yesterday, before we even start to begin to meet today's targets.

That is why Reform wants practical planning reforms, making it easier to create desperately needed homes above high-street shops, seriously restricting the conversion of hotels into HMOs and relieving the burden on overwhelmed planning and housing teams. But while we build for the future, we must also be honest about the homes that we have now and who should have first call on them. This motion proposes a sensible and proportionate measure. It will help ensure that the scarce resource of social homes are available first to the people with the strongest claim on them. This is a principle that this Senedd should be able to support, and I urge Members to do so. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Clywsom gyfraniadau pwysig gan gyd-Aelodau. Cynigiodd Joe Martin syniad y byddai llawer ar ochrau eraill y Siambr yn falch o'i weld, rwy'n siŵr: ef yn symud i Tsieina. [Chwerthin.] Fodd bynnag, pe bai'n symud yno, byddai'n rhaid iddo ddod o hyd i'w dŷ ei hun. Ni fyddai'n cael cartref ar geiniog gwladwriaeth Tsieina. Ein cyfrifoldeb moesol ni yw rhoi pobl Cymru a Phrydain yn gyntaf. Tynnodd John Clark sylw, yn gywir ddigon, at y ffaith ei bod yn annheg y gall unigolyn sydd wedi talu trethi i'n gwlad ers degawdau fod yn aros yn hwy am dŷ na'r rhai sydd newydd gyrraedd. A rhannodd Francesca O'Brien ffigurau difrifol—[Torri ar draws.] Rwy'n credu ein bod wedi cael digon o ymyriadau heddiw, diolch. Rhannodd ffigurau difrifol yn tynnu sylw at raddfa'r mater hwn a diffyg tryloywder rhai awdurdodau lleol.

Hoffwn roi eiliad i ymateb i rai o'r sylwadau eraill a wnaed, gan ddechrau gydag arweinydd Llafur Cymru. Er eglurder, ganwyd Suella Braverman yn Llundain ac mae'n ddinesydd Prydeinig, felly byddai ganddi hawl i dŷ cymdeithasol o dan y polisi hwn. Peter—[Torri ar draws.] Peter, fel rwyf newydd egluro, nid yw dinasyddion yr UE yn cael eu heffeithio gan y polisi hwn pan fydd ganddynt statws preswylwyr sefydlog, er bod yn rhaid imi ddweud ei bod yn anodd derbyn gwersi gan y Torïaid am ddifrifoldeb mewn perthynas â mewnfudo. Kiera, mae'r hawl i brynu—[Torri ar draws.] Mae'r hawl i brynu yn rhoi cyfle i bobl fod yn berchen ar eu cartref eu hunain, un o'r cydraddolwyr cyfoeth mwyaf y mae'r wlad hon wedi'u gweld erioed. Nawr, a ellir gwneud hyn yn wahanol? Wrth gwrs y gellir ei wneud yn wahanol. Ond gall gwerthu un tŷ cymdeithasol roi'r ecwiti ichi adeiladu tri arall. Mae dweud yn syml na fyddwn yn caniatáu—[Torri ar draws.] Mae dweud yn syml na fyddwn yn caniatáu i deuluoedd sy'n gweithio gael cyfle i gamu ar yr ysgol dai a bod yn berchen ar eu cartref eu hunain yn nonsens. Jayne, nid yw dweud y dylai Llywodraeth Cymru roi pobl Cymru yn gyntaf yn ymrannol. Ac i arweinydd Plaid Werdd Cymru, nid oes unrhyw beth hyllach a mwy atgas na'ch plaid chi'n datgan bod credu y gall gwladwriaeth Israel fodoli yn hiliol.

Wrth gwrs, nid diwygio dyraniadau'n unig yw'r ateb cyfan. Mae angen inni adeiladu mwy o gartrefi, ond yma hefyd, mae Cymru ar ei cholled. Weinidog, fe sonioch chi am bwysigrwydd adeiladu tai. Fodd bynnag, rydym wedi rhannu rhwystredigaethau gyda'r system gynllunio yn ddiweddar iawn. Mae penderfyniadau cynllunio'n cymryd misoedd ac weithiau blynyddoedd, gan ohirio buddsoddiad ac adeiladu tai. Yn hytrach na gweithredu nawr i leddfu'r pwysau ar adrannau cynllunio, mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi dechrau adolygiad tair blynedd o'r fframwaith cynllunio cenedlaethol. Ni all Cymru fforddio tair blynedd arall o fod ar ei hôl hi. Mae'r ôl-groniad eisoes yn ddifrifol. Mae Sefydliad Bevan yn amcangyfrif bod Cymru oddeutu 9,600 o gartrefi yn brin. Mae hynny'n cyfateb i adeiladu Llandudno arall, Bangor arall, adeiladu Rhyl arall bron iawn. Roedd angen y cartrefi hyn ddoe, cyn inni hyd yn oed ddechrau cyrraedd targedau heddiw.

Dyna pam y mae Reform eisiau diwygiadau cynllunio ymarferol, gan ei gwneud yn haws i greu cartrefi y mae eu hangen yn ddirfawr uwchben siopau'r stryd fawr, cyfyngu'n ddifrifol ar drosi gwestai yn dai amlfeddiannaeth a lleddfu'r baich ar dimau cynllunio a thai sydd wedi'u gorlethu. Ond wrth inni adeiladu ar gyfer y dyfodol, rhaid inni hefyd fod yn onest am y cartrefi sydd gennym nawr ac i bwy y dylid eu cynnig gyntaf. Mae'r cynnig hwn yn argymell mesur synhwyrol a chymesur. Bydd yn helpu i sicrhau bod adnodd prin tai cymdeithasol ar gael yn gyntaf i'r bobl sydd â'r hawl gryfaf iddynt. Mae hon yn egwyddor y dylai'r Senedd hon allu ei chefnogi, ac rwy'n annog yr Aelodau i wneud hynny. Diolch.

Felly, cyfnod pleidleisio: eitem 6—dadl Aelodau. Galwaf am bleidlais ar y cynnig, dadl Aelodau o dan Reol Sefydlog 11.21(iv), llysoedd cyffuriau ac alcohol teuluol. Galwaf am bleidlais ar y cynnig a gyflwynwyd yn enw Tom Montgomery, Natasha Asghar, Jane Dodds a Sarah Cooper-Lesadd. Agorwch y bleidlais. Caewch y bleidlais. XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
That brings us to voting time. Unless five Members wish for the bell to be rung, I will proceed directly to voting time. Excellent, thank you.

So, we will first vote on item 6—Member debate. I call for a vote on the motion under Standing Order 11.21(iv), family drug and alcohol courts. I call for a vote on the motion tabled in the name of Tom Montgomery, Natasha Asghar, Jane Dodds and Sarah Cooper-Lesadd. Open the vote. Close the vote. The result of the vote is as follows: in favour 71, 16 abstentions and none against. The motion is therefore agreed.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cynnig NDM9313 fel y'i diwygiwyd:

Cynnig bod y Senedd: 

1. Yn nodi bod tai cymdeithasol yn cael eu dyrannu gan awdurdodau lleol yn unol â deddfwriaeth a chynlluniau dyrannu lleol, gyda blaenoriaeth yn cael ei phennu yn ôl yr angen am dai a chategorïau blaenoriaeth statudol. 

2. Yn cydnabod bod cymhwysedd ar gyfer tai cymdeithasol a chymorth digartrefedd yn cael ei lywodraethu gan ddeddfwriaeth, gan gynnwys darpariaethau sy'n ymwneud â statws mewnfudo a phreswyliad cyfreithlon yn y Deyrnas Unedig. 

3. Yn credu bod penderfyniadau sy'n ymwneud â thrwyddedu a rheoli tai amlfeddiannaeth yn cael eu gwneud orau gan awdurdodau lleol o fewn y fframwaith a sefydlwyd gan ddeddfwriaeth a chanllawiau Llywodraeth Cymru. 

4. Yn nodi bod penderfyniadau ynghylch gwasgariad a llety pobl sy'n ceisio lloches yn cael eu cadw i Lywodraeth y DU ac yn credu y dylai trefniadau gwasgaru effeithiol ystyried capasiti lleol, effaith debygol ar gydlyniant cymunedol a’r gwasanaethau cymorth sydd ar gael. 

5. Yn cefnogi ymgysylltu rhwng Llywodraeth Cymru a Llywodraeth y DU i hyrwyddo trefniadau gwasgaru teg a chynaliadwy ac i gefnogi integreiddio a chydlyniant cymunedol llwyddiannus ledled Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Motion NDM9313 as amended:

To propose that the Senedd: 

1. Notes social housing is allocated by local authorities in accordance with legislation and local allocation schemes, with priority determined by housing need and statutory priority categories. 

2. Recognises eligibility for social housing and homelessness assistance is governed by legislation, including provisions relating to immigration status and lawful residence in the United Kingdom. 

3. Believes decisions relating to the licensing and management of houses in multiple occupation are best taken by local authorities within the framework established by legislation and Welsh Government guidance. 

4. Notes decisions regarding the dispersal of and accommodation for people seeking asylum are reserved to the UK Government and believes that effective dispersal arrangements should take account of local capacity, likely impact on community cohesion and the availability of support services. 

5. Supports engagement between the Welsh Government and the UK Government to promote fair and sustainable dispersal arrangements and to support successful integration and community cohesion across Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 10. Dadl Fer: Pwysigrwydd seilwaith porthladdoedd a thraffig morwrol i economi Cymru
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 10. Short Debate: The importance of port infrastructure and maritime traffic to the Welsh economy
